Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank 9 june 1998 ladies and gentlemen i am here today to report on the outcome of the first meetings of the three decisionmaking bodies of the ecb the general council the governing council and the executive board all of which in accordance with the escbecb statute are chaired by me as president of the ecb or in my absence by the vicepresident who is sitting next to me

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i may recall that the heads of state or government appointed six members to the executive board of the ecb including the president and the vicepresident as from 1 june 1998 which thus constitutes the date of establishment not only of the ecb but also of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i may also recall that on 4 june 1998 the executive board released a press statement announcing its 2 june 1998 decision on the distribution of responsibilities among its members for the business areas of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in subsequent meetings of the executive board the first meetings of the governing and the general councils were prepared

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the first meetings of both bodies were held earlier today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further information about the members of the decisionmaking bodies of the ecb about the constitution of the escb about its objectives and tasks and about its organisation has been made available in a press folder and can also be found on the ecbs web site section about the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the general council which includes all fifteen eu national central bank governors provisionally adopted its own rules of procedure

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: they will be formally approved at the next meeting of the general council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in accordance with article 47 of the escbecb statute the general council also made a contribution to the decisionmaking of the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for this reason the general council met before the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the contribution consisted in delivering opinions on two important institutional matters i the key for the subscription of the capital of the ecb ii the conditions of employment of ecb staff

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the end of its meeting the general council agreed for the remainder of this year to meet on 1 september 1998 and on 1 december 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: following the meeting of the general council the governing council met for the first time in its composition of the six members of the executive board and the governors of the eleven national central banks of the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: mr de silguy participated in the meeting as a member of the european commission the president of the eu council who also has a right to attend did not participate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council i took note of the rules of procedure of the european central bank as proposed by the executive board and will revert to them at its next meeting ii it adopted three decisions the first decision relates to the method to be applied for determining the national central banks percentage shares in the key for the ecbs capital

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: application of this method has resulted in shares for the fifteen eu national central banks being determined with a level of precision of four decimal places i will not read out the details however this information is being made available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the second decision relates to the measures necessary for the paying up of the capital of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it has been decided that the eleven national central banks of the euro area will pay up in full their respective subscriptions to the ecbs capital according to the key established in the preceding decision and that they will do so by 1 july 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as a result the ecb will be endowed with an initial capital of slightly under eur 4 billion the third decision consists in recommending to the council of the european union the first external auditor of the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these and future decisions will obviously be published in the official journal of the european communities for general notice

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also decided on a number of organisational matters i it laid down the conditions of employment of the staff of the european central bank ii it provisionally agreed on a budget for the european central bank for the second half of 1998 which will be formally adopted at the next meeting iii it agreed on the framework for the organisation of the overall testing of escbwide systems and procedures which will be conducted in the second half of this year so as to ensure that the escb is in a position to undertake its tasks as from 1 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: furthermore the governing council decided on two specific issues relating to the preparation of stage three i with respect to the target system a pricing policy was agreed the main element of which is the degressive tariff that will be applied to payment transactions flowing through this system

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a separate press release which will be made available in all community languages will provide further details on this matter ii with respect to the euro banknotes a largely decentralised approach for the initial supply of such banknotes has been agreed upon

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this means that each of the eleven national central banks of the euro area will be free to organise the industrial process for the production of the euro banknotes needed to replace their national banknotes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in other words each national central bank may produce all of the relevant euro banknotes itself or alternatively it may enter into bilateral pooling arrangements

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the governing council was consulted by the executive board on the organisational structure of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council took note of and agreed with this structure information about which is being made available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also agreed with the proposals of the executive board as regards the appointment of ecb managers

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should like to point out that of the fiftyfive managerial positions in the ecb fortynine will be recruited from the current emi staff

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: finally the governing council decided for the remainder of this year to meet in any event on the first tuesday of every month with the exception of the month of august

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: thus the next meeting of the governing council is scheduled for 7 july 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: before that date more precisely on 30 june 1998 there will be a ceremony to be held in the alte oper in frankfurt to mark the establishment of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the remainder of this year the governing council will have to decide on all elements of the socalled regulatory organisational and logistical framework necessary for the escb to perform its tasks in stage three which the emi has prepared in accordance with the treaty

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: to this end the executive board is currently preparing a work programme which will cover inter alia such items as i the decision on whether or not to introduce a minimum reserve system and the specification of its features ii the monetary policy strategy iii the procedural rules for the administration of erm2 iv the transfer of foreign reserve assets to the ecb v the provision of intraday liquidity to noneuro area national central banks of the eu in the target system vi the technical specification for the euro banknotes vii the scope and format of the financial reporting of the escb viii the allocation of the escbs monetary income

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: you will understand that after nine days of ecb existence i am not yet in a position to give you further details on the precise timing of the decisionmaking on the above and many other items to be addressed by the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank wednesday 8 july 1998 ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of the second meeting of the governing council of the european central bank held yesterday

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council first assessed current economic developments in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the general picture is one of continued economic expansion combined with broadly low inflation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: several forecasts made during spring 1998 have even suggested slightly lower rates of inflation for 199899 compared with expectations in autumn 1997

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as far as price developments are concerned inflation as measured by the harmonised consumer price index hicp is estimated to have risen slightly in april to 14 but has not increased further in may

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: output growth has remained strong in recent quarters with annual growth rates close to or even exceeding 3

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: economic growth has been driven increasingly by domestic demand rather than net exports as might be expected at this stage of the cycle

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: private consumption and stockbuilding have been the main factors underlying domestic demand to date

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the favourable conjunctural situation has started to feed through into the labour market although improvements here have in some countries been too slow to appear

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is evident however that economic growth alone will not reduce the urgency to proceed with structural adjustments in order to tackle unacceptably high rates of unemployment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards monetary and financial developments in the euro area the annual growth rate of the broad money supply m3h accelerated in april to around 6 from 55 in march

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the growth rate of m1 the narrow money supply also picked up to around 10

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we shall monitor these developments very carefully

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in principle the economic performance i have just described provides a favourable environment for continued fiscal consolidation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is with some concern that we observe that in a number of member countries the prospects for this to actually develop seem to be to put it mildly rather subdued

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this respect i should like to underline three aspects

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first any growth dividend resulting from the current cyclical upturn should be used to bring deficit and debt levels down rather than relaxing control over expenditure

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second most member states need to go a step further and indeed improve structural balances as they are not yet in compliance with the obligations under the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this implies that the benchmark for fiscal policy must now be a budget close to balance or in surplus in surplus especially in countries with high ratios of debt to gdp

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: third further structural adjustments in fiscal policy would also help to improve the policy mix in some countries and in the euro area as a whole from the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i would not at the present time want to try to convey too strong an impression of the implications of these various economic developments for the appropriate stance of monetary policies in euro area member states

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: although the responsibility for these policies remains with national central banks until the end of this year the governing council had an extensive and thorough discussion on a euro area perspective of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we will continue to study this issue closely before we enter the regime of a single monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the time being it is encouraging to see the credibility of monetary policy being reflected in the exchange rates of euro countries

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: there is currently no sign of exchange rate tensions among euro area currencies

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: forward exchange rates are expected to be virtually identical to central rates suggesting that the preannounced rates are considered credible

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i consider this a remarkable achievement

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: following its review of economic developments the governing council settled a number of organisational issues

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it adopted the rules of procedure of the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these will be published in the official journal of the european communities it approved in accordance with the rules of procedure the establishment of eleven escb committees to assist in the work of the european system of central banks escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the committees are as follows listed in alphabetical order accounting and monetary income committee banking supervision committee banknote committee external communications committee information technology committee internal auditors committee legal committee market operations committee monetary policy committee payment and settlement systems committee and statistics committee it formally adopted a budget for the european central bank for the second half of 1998 and agreed on the establishment of a budget committee to assist the governing council in ecb budgetrelated matters it laid down specific rules applicable to staff transferring from the european monetary institute to the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: ecb decisions relating to the conditions of employment will be published in the official journal of the european communities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also took a number of decisions relating to various aspects of its preparatory work for stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a monetary policy issues the governing council decided on the introduction of a minimum reserve system by the escb at the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: among the three main functions that a minimum reserve system could usefully perform the governing council attaches particularly high importance to its contributions to the stabilisation of money market interest rates and to the enlargement of the demand for central bank money by creating or enlarging a structural liquidity shortage in the market

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the light of the potential burden which a minimum reserve system could impose on the private sector and the effects it might have on the financial activity of credit institutions in the euro area the governing council has decided on features which fulfil the two money market management purposes outlined above while at the same time allowing an adequate remuneration of minimum reserves

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a number of details of the minimum reserve system that will be applied were already specified in previous documents published by the european monetary institute

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: additional features agreed upon yesterday include the liability base the lumpsum allowance and the rate of remuneration

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to the latter the ecb will remunerate minimum reserve holdings at a level corresponding to the rate of its main refinancing operations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council intends to decide on the exact specification of the minimum reserve system in november 1998 at the latest

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this decision in particular as regards the reserve ratio which is currently defined within a range of 15 25 will be based on the early data from the new system for money and banking statistics

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details are provided in the separate press release that is being issued to you this morning

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is intended that the precise features of the minimum reserve system will be published in the form of an eu council regulation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for this purpose the governing council adopted an ecb recommendation for an eu council regulation on the application of minimum reserves by the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in accordance with the provisions of the statute of the escb the eu council acting by a qualified majority and after consulting the european parliament and the commission is expected to adopt this regulation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also adopted ecb recommendations for eu council regulations concerning the collection of statistical information by the ecb and concerning the powers of the ecb to impose sanctions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: all three ecb recommendations will be published in the official journal of the european communities for general notice

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: b foreign exchange issues the governing council decided on the size and form of the initial transfer of foreign reserve assets to the european central bank from the national central banks participating in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this transfer is to take place on the first day of 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it has been decided that the initial transfer will be to the maximum allowed amount of eur 50 billion adjusted downwards by deducting the shares in the ecbs capital subscription key of the eu central banks which will not participate in the euro area at the outset

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the transfer will thus be equal to 789153 of eur 50 billion ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: approximately eur 3946 billion

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council furthermore agreed that this initial transfer should be in gold in an amount equivalent to 15 of the sum i have just mentioned with the remaining 85 being transferred in foreign currency assets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should stress that the decision on the percentage of gold to be transferred to the ecb will have no implications for the consolidated gold holdings of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the precise modalities of the initial transfer will be finalised before the end of the year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: before the end of the current year the governing council will also have to adopt an ecb guideline pursuant to article 313 of the statute of the escb which will subject all operations in foreign reserve assets remaining with the national central banks including gold to approval by the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in connection with the settingup of common market standards the governing council also reached agreement on a number of issues related to the quotation and publication of reference exchange rates for the euro

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: specifically it was agreed to recommend to market participants the certain method for quoting the exchange rates for the euro ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 1 euro x foreign currency units and to have daily reference exchange rates for the euro computed and published by the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: c payment systems issues the governing council decided on the conditions for the participation of the noneuro area eu central banks and credit institutions in the target transeuropean automated realtime gross settlement express transfer system

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in target the escb will provide central bank liquidity in the course of the day ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: intraday liquidity to the extent necessary to avoid delays in the execution of payment orders

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: if intraday liquidity is not reimbursed at the end of the day it becomes overnight credit granted by the escb which for evident monetary policy reasons cannot be offered to institutions outside the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: nonetheless noneuro area eu central banks and institutions in those countries will be connected to target

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council considered that giving such institutions outside the euro area unlimited access to intraday credit would have created risks for the conduct of monetary policy that it was not ready to take

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a facility will therefore be put in place to enable the noneuro area eu central banks to provide collateralised intraday credit in euro to their credit institutions subject to a ceiling both at the level of the noneuro area eu central banks and at that of noneuro area credit institutions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: there will also be a liquidity deadline set at 5 pm for noneuro area credit institutions so that they do not incur an overnight overdraft in euro

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also agreed that a report on recent developments in the field of electronic money and their monetary policy implications would be published in september 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: d legal protection of euro banknotes finally the governing council agreed on a number of legal instruments aimed at enhancing the protection of euro banknotes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular an ecb decision on the denominations specifications reproduction exchange and withdrawal of banknotes has been adopted as well as an ecb recommendation regarding the adoption of certain measures to enhance the legal protection of euro banknotes and coins

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: both documents will be published for general information in the official journal of the european communities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we are at your disposal for further questions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report not only on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council of the european central bank but also as you are already aware on the outcome of the meetings of the governing council and the general council that took place on 1 september 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it was in view of the short time span between the two sets of meetings that we decided that it would be more efficient to hold only one press conference to provide you with a summary of our deliberations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is my intention to continue this practice for the remaining meetings of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this regard the governing council will meet not only as scheduled on 13 october 3 november and 1 december 1998 but there will also be an additional meeting on tuesday 22 december 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: by this time the bulk of nearly five years of preparatory work including the emi years will be behind us and i envisage that the governing councils final meeting before the start of stage three of economic and monetary union emu will be devoted to finetuning its lastminute preparations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: you will recall that monetary policy decisions remain a national competence until 31 december 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: looking ahead to next year the governing council will hold fortnightly meetings and i intend to hold a press conference normally once a month

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the first quarter of 1999 i envisage holding a press conference immediately after the first meeting of each month

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details of the meetings schedule are provided in the separate press release that will be issued to you this evening

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me however return to the present

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council and the general council devoted part of their september meetings to an extended exchange of views on recent economic monetary and financial developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular much attention was paid to the global economic and financial environment of the future euro area which has clearly worsened

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: two major factors are currently affecting capital markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first the flight into quality

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second and related the tendency to switch from equities to bonds

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as evidenced once again over the past few days by large swings in investor sentiment the monetary policy environment has become more uncertain

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: one focal aspect of the discussion has been a close monitoring of the financial crisis in russia

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as we all know the russian crisis has added to concerns regarding the state of the world economy at a time when the crisis in asia is still ongoing and growth in japan is negative

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these concerns have been fuelled by renewed strains in international financial markets as well as sharp fluctuations and downward corrections in major stock markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: there is no doubt that these developments will have a dampening effect on the world economy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however their precise impact is difficult to measure at the current juncture

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the one hand economic and modelbased analysis still suggests only moderate effects on prices and output in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this is due to the fact that first most of the crisis regions are quite small in economic terms ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: when compared with world gdp or their contribution to world trade

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second trade links between these countries and the euro area are also of limited size

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: third the euro area itself is a very large economy which is only directly exposed to variations in global trade to a certain degree

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however on the other hand this analysis should not mislead us

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we are perfectly aware that the risks associated with current global developments go beyond those effects which we can measure directly

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this respect one may think of indirect influences resulting from changes in confidence saving and expenditure within the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we have to take these risks seriously and analyse the situation soberly but we should also not dramatise

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me now turn to the latest available data

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these seem to indicate that economic expansion within the euro area has remained broadly on track despite the worsening of the external environment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: domestic demand remains strong while the contribution to growth from net exports has declined

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: both private consumption and investment provided an important stimulus to the growth rate in the first quarter of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: more uptodate indicators point towards continued expansion in the second quarter albeit at a possibly more moderate pace than in the first quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outlook on consumption is supported by higher real earnings growth and declining unemployment and is reflected in consumer confidence

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the evidence for the corporate sector is perhaps more mixed

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as compared to the first quarter of 1998 industrial production figures show a somewhat slower rate of increase in the period from april to may but capacity utilisation has continued to increase and this combined with low interest rates should underpin investment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: european commission survey data such as confidence indicators and the assessment of order books bear witness to relatively high levels both with respect to their longterm averages and recent peaks

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this can also be taken as a favourable indicator for continued growth in the short term although some indicators have not improved further since the spring

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: unemployment has also been declining but at a modest pace and from a high level

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in discussing the cyclical uncertainties one should not forget that work on badly needed structural reforms has not so far made much progress

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: considering recent price developments hicp inflation for the euro area as a whole remained stable at 14 between may and july

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: both domestic and external factors still appear to be favourable suggesting that euro area inflation may be expected to remain subdued in the future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: an important external factor underlying the favourable prospects for inflation is the sharp decline in oil and commodity prices which is partly associated with developments in asia

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover domestic sources of inflation such as those arising from the labour market situation and capacity utilisation are also relatively moderate at the present juncture

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in my opinion taking a euro area wide perspective these views are also broadly compatible with current monetary and financial developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this connection please take note that we should soon have new information on monetary developments on the basis of the new statistical reporting framework for money and banking

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the environment of significant volatility in international financial markets particularly stock markets appears to account for much of the recent decline in longterm interest rates in the euro area to historically low levels as investors have sought to protect themselves against heightened global risk

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: nonetheless it is notable that the euro area yield curve shifted downwards at all maturities which to some extent would tend to indicate a further decline in longterm inflation expectations for the euro area as a whole

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as we approach the start of stage three we shall need to continue to monitor closely economic monetary and financial developments within the euro area and in the world economy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this will allow us eventually to set the interest rate for the euro area as a whole

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time we shall also need to monitor fiscal intentions in the euro area member states as they will become more transparent over the autumn

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: if governments merely adhere to previous deficit targets for 1999 the structural position of budgets in quite a number of countries would effectively deteriorate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this would entail that they would move farther away from rather than approach the requirements of the stability and growth pact which calls for the achievement of a budget close to balance or even in surplus

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition to the review of economic developments a number of organisational issues were settled

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i the general council adopted its rules of procedure which will be published in the official journal of the european communities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: you will recall that i informed you that the governing councils rules of procedure were adopted in july

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: ii the general council also decided that the noneuro area national central banks shall pay up 5 of their subscriptions to the capital of the european central bank ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the four national central banks concerned will not be asked actually to pay in their share as the amount due is less than they can expect to receive as their share in the proceeds of the liquidation of the european monetary institute emi

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details on the actual amounts involved are provided in the separate handout that will be issued to you this evening

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: iii for its part the governing council completed the list of committees which will assist in the work of the european system of central banks escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition to the eleven escb committees agreed upon at the meeting in july the governing council decided to establish an international relations committee and a budget committee

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: ladies and gentlemen in line with our stated intention the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council of the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the length of my introductory statement reflects the importance of the matters dealt with today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as usual the governing council devoted part of its meeting to an exchange of views on recent economic monetary and financial developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this discussion took place against the background of conflicting messages

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: clearly on the one hand the data on the economic situation in the united states and europe especially in the euro area mainly indicate a continuation of real gdp growth though possibly at a somewhat slower pace

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the other hand however the global macroeconomic environment has deteriorated

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular the number of signs suggesting that the world economy will slow down in 1999 is increasing

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time uncertainty in the financial markets has been heightened by news of the near collapse of a large hedge fund losses by individual financial institutions and the large movements in world equity bond and foreign exchange markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council in responding to recent economic developments and current market conditions it is of the utmost importance that proposals inspired by policy activism that do not take due account of the complexity of the issues at stake are avoided

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this would only contribute to compounding the uncertainties which underlie the prevailing global financial market volatility

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the governing council is of the view that proposals for a reassessment of capital controls as an acceptable policy option or recent calls for worldwide uniform interest rate reductions are inappropriate as they do not address the very nature of the problems

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time the governing council considers structural improvements at the global level to be warranted

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these should focus in particular first on enhancing the transparency of both the public and private sectors second on strengthening domestic banking systems primarily in emerging markets and economies in transition and third on improving financial crisis prevention and management in particular through the increased involvement of the private sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a number of proposals have already been developed on these issues which should now be finalised with a view to their early and forceful implementation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the governing council stressed that such structural improvements at the global level would have to be accompanied by sound policies at home

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this respect given the size of the euro area and its global role it is of crucial importance that price stability and hence a climate conducive to growth and employment should be maintained in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: achieving this will also be of vital importance for the world economy as a whole

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with this in mind the governing council reviewed the monetary financial and macroeconomic situation in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first the council discussed the monetary situation with reference to preliminary data on the basis of the new harmonised reporting system for money and banking statistics

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: once internal work has been completed these monetary statistics will be made available to the public

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: when looking at various definitions of broad money our preliminary data show broadly similar and stable annual growth rates of between 3 and 5 in 1997 and the first half of 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: according to our initial analysis these data do not appear to signal inflationary pressures arising from money at this juncture

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however given the preliminary nature of the new data caution should be exercised with regard to their interpretation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second as regards other financial indicators although longterm interest rates have risen recently they are still at low levels by historical standards and the yield curve has levelled off relative to the situation some months ago

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a substantial part of developments in bond markets during recent months reflects a flight into quality

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: third the governing council discussed the broad outlook for prices in the context of the overall macroeconomic environment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with respect to price developments international factors continued to exert downward pressure

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: hicp rates in the euro area fell to 12 in august after having remained unchanged at 14 from april to july

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this mainly reflected a decline in energy prices which were almost 4 lower in august than a year earlier and in other commodity prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the euro area as a whole price pressure as indicated by industrial output prices and labour costs also remained modest

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in 1999 average inflation in the euro area is expected to remain subdued according to the projections available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: fourth considerable difficulties are encountered in precisely assessing and quantifying the impact of recent international developments on prices and equally on activity

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: recent data seem to suggest that real gdp growth in the euro area which reached 06 in the first quarter of 1998 has slowed down somewhat in the second quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we need to await the release of more complete and thereby more reliable data for the euro area as a whole before a final view can be taken

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: other recently released data on industrial production the volume of retail sales and passenger car registrations appear to point to continued growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this view is also supported by ec survey data although some indicators have remained constant or have fallen back slightly in recent months nonetheless all these indicators remain well above their longterm averages

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council welcomed recent interest rate reductions by a number of euro area national central banks

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as a result euro areawide threemonth interest rates have now reached a level of 38 which implies a decrease of around 15 basis points since the end of august

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these changes underline the fact that the process of the convergence of central bank interest rates in the euro area which is to be concluded by the end of this year is clearly under way

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council considered further interest rate convergence towards the lower end of the current range prevailing in the euro area as being appropriate given our current knowledge of monetary trends and the prospects for price developments and taking account of an environment characterised by risks of downward pressures

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council will continue to monitor closely monetary financial and economic developments within the euro area with a view to determining the appropriate level of money market interest rates for the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: meanwhile the governing council will continue to monitor closely fiscal intentions in the euro area member states

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the structural budgetary positions in several member states are still far from being close to balance or in surplus as required by the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore these member states are not yet sufficiently prepared to enable automatic stabilisers to function in the event of a slowdown in real gdp growth while still respecting the 3 reference value set out in the treaty and ensuring a decline of debt ratios at an appropriate pace

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover in a number of member states against the background of a still favourable and partly better than expected growth performance shortterm budgetary targets appear not to represent structural improvements

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition to the review of economic developments a number of decisions were taken with regard to various aspects of the preparatory work for stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a monetary policy issues first and foremost let me turn to the issue of the monetary policy strategy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i can inform you that at todays meeting the governing council reached agreement on the main features of the stabilityoriented monetary policy strategy that the escb will pursue in stage three of monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: before explaining our decision on the strategy let me emphasise certain important characteristics of the environment in which the single monetary policy will operate as of next january

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: of most concern to the escb are some uncertainties which will inevitably arise as a result of the move to stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these relate in particular to the way in which the transition to stage three of monetary union will affect economic behaviour and institutional and financial structures in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: they also relate to statistical issues

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the governing council has chosen a distinct monetary policy strategy one that reflects the special circumstances it faces at present

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this strategy will ensure continuity with the successful strategies pursued by participating national central banks in recent years while taking into account to the extent needed the unique situation created by the transition to monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with this context in mind the governing council today agreed on the main elements of the stabilityoriented monetary policy strategy of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these elements concern the quantitative definition of the primary objective of the single monetary policy price stability a prominent role for money with a reference value for the growth of a monetary aggregate and a broadlybased assessment of the outlook for future price developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first let me stress that as mandated by the treaty establishing the european community the maintenance of price stability will be the primary objective of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore the escbs monetary policy strategy will focus strictly on this objective

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the interest of transparency and in order to give clear guidance with regard to expectations regarding future price developments the governing council of the ecb has agreed to announce a quantitative definition of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this context the governing council of the ecb has adopted the following definition price stability shall be defined as a yearonyear increase in the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp for the euro area of below 2

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me emphasise the fact that price stability is an objective which is to be maintained over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the current rate of hicp inflation in the euro area is in line with this objective

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: three features of this definition should be highlighted first the hicp is the most appropriate price measure for the escbs definition of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is the only price index that will be sufficiently harmonised across the euro area at the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second by defining price stability using the hicp for the euro area the governing council of the ecb makes it clear that it will base its decisions on monetary economic and financial developments in the euro area as a whole

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should like to emphasise the fact that the single monetary policy will adopt a euro areawide perspective it will not react to specific regional or national developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: third this definition is very much in line with most current definitions adopted by national central banks in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: furthermore the statement that price stability is to be maintained over the medium term reflects the need for monetary policy to have a forwardlooking mediumterm orientation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it also acknowledges the existence of shortterm volatility in prices which cannot be controlled by monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in order to maintain price stability the governing council of the ecb agreed to adopt a monetary policy strategy which will consist of two key elements

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: deviations of current monetary growth from the reference value would under normal circumstances signal risks to price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the escb will assess how best to counter these risks

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the concept of a reference value does not imply a commitment on the part of the escb to mechanistically correct deviations of monetary growth from the reference value over the short termthe relationship between actual monetary growth and the preannounced reference value will be regularly and thoroughly analysed by the governing council of the ecb the result of this analysis and its impact on monetary policy decisions will be explained to the public

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the precise definition of the reference aggregate and the specific value of the quantitative reference value for monetary growth will be announced by the governing council of the ecb in december 1998however while the monetary aggregates contain important and relevant information for monetary policymaking monetary developments will not constitute a complete summary of all the information about the economy that needs to be known for an appropriate monetary policy to be set

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: thus the governing council will systematically analyse all the information available regarding the prospects for and the risks to price stability in the euro area as a whole

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this strategy underlines the strong commitment of the governing council of the ecb to its primary objective and should facilitate the achievement of this overriding goal

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it will also ensure the transparency of the escbs decisionmaking and its accountability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: based on its strategy the governing council of the ecb will inform the public regularly and in detail about its assessment of the monetary economic and financial situation in the euro area and the reasoning behind its specific policy decisions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this strategy is designed to avoid giving the impression that monetary policy responds mechanistically to deviations from a single target or changes to a specific variable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the monetary policy strategy that has been selected by the governing council of the ecb signals that monetary policy in the euro area will be determined in a manner which will maintain price stability responding to new developments in or disturbances to the economy in an appropriate manner which is consistent with this overriding objective

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the strategy therefore offers a clear and transparent framework within which the governing council of the ecb will be able to assess and present monetary policy decisions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: please note that the main features of the strategy are also summarised in a press release to be distributed to you

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: still in the context of preparing for the single monetary policy you may recall that in july i informed you about the range of institutions subject to reserve requirements and the liabilities included in the reserve base

Parsed_Text: for nonmonetary policy transactions it will for instance also be possible to process payments via the eba euro clearing system currently the ecu clearing and settlement system

Parsed_Text: d the euro banknotes with a view to increasing efficiency in combating counterfeiting the governing council confirmed the agreement reached by the emi council that a currency analysis centre and a counterfeit currency database will be set up which will store technical data relating to counterfeit euro banknotes
