Parsed_Text: ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meetings of the governing council and the general council of the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: similarly to last month the governing council had a very heavy agenda with many of the items being of a rather technical nature or related to the legal implementation of decisions already taken at previous meetings

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: today the governing council focused inter alia on various projections available for the world economy and the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this material pointed unequivocally to some deceleration of real gdp growth in the euro area in 1999 compared with the widely expected growth rate of just below 3 in 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the governing council took note of the apparently calmer conditions in world financial markets in november this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a key feature has been the diminished volatility in financial markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the governing council pointed out that caution is warranted when interpreting the most recent developments and the projections available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed downward risks continue to exist

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council apart from global developments the most significant risk for all forecasts is that confidence within the euro area and thereby domestic demand could be negatively affected

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: confidence in the corporate sector has already declined

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this respect the governing council emphasised the utmost importance of maintaining a sound and sustainable policy framework within the euro area particularly in the interest of supporting confidence

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this framework is characterised by the maintenance of a stabilityoriented monetary policy a conduct of fiscal policies which is consistent with the stability and growth pact and ongoing structural reforms in the labour and product markets accompanied by continued wage moderation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: maintaining this policy framework will help to foster competitiveness and profitability in the corporate sector thereby promoting investment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: equally it will help to sustain and foster the employment growth that has been seen recently thereby supporting private consumption

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the governing council discussed in depth issues related to the conduct of monetary policy for the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me elaborate on that discussion which further prepared the ground for the setting of interest rates for the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the context of the stabilityoriented monetary policy strategy the main elements of which were announced in october this year the governing council agreed on the quantitative reference value for monetary growth and the monetary aggregate to which it applies

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover the governing council carefully analysed the data on monetary developments and made a thorough examination of the broad outlook for price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the first reference value for monetary growth decided by the governing council which plays a prominent role in the governing councils monetary policy assessment will apply to the broad monetary aggregate m3 and has been set at an annual rate of 4 12 it will be reviewed in december 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this rate is consistent with the maintenance of price stability according to the escbs published definition while allowing for sustainable output growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it has been derived by assuming that the trend growth rate of real gdp in the euro area is in the range of 2 to 2 12 per annum and the velocity of circulation of m3 declines at a trend rate of between 12 and 1 each year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details related to the derivation of the reference rate and the definition of the broad aggregate m3 are described in a separate press statement to be released today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to the reference value let me stress two points very clearly

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first the reference value for m3 growth has been derived in an explicit mediumterm context in line with the escbs monetary policy strategy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: analysis of monetary developments relative to the reference value will provide a firm anchor for the conduct of the stabilityoriented single monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second the escbs monetary policy strategy does not entail mechanistic policy reactions to deviations of monetary growth from the announced reference value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the first instance deviations of monetary growth will be analysed thoroughly in parallel with the broadly based assessment of the outlook for price developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: preliminary estimates for part of the euro area indicate that the average of the 12month growth rates for the last three months including october was around 45

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: taking a mediumterm perspective the governing council took note of the fact that over the last two years the annual rate of m3 growth has constantly fluctuated in a range of 35 to 55

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it was concluded that this monetary trend appears to be broadly compatible with continued price stability in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in line with the escbs monetary policy strategy the governing council will closely monitor developments in m3 in relation to the reference value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards other financial indicators average longterm interest rates in the euro area declined slightly in november to 415

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the decline in longterm interest rates which has been substantial since june this year is consistent with the view that markets currently have low inflation expectations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the discussion on the appropriate interest rates for the start of stage three was further deepened during the deliberations of the members of the governing council on the broad outlook for price stability in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: prospects for price developments are generally seen as favourable as the rate of increase in the hicp which stood at 10 in october is expected to remain below 2 in the foreseeable future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however this is conditional on import prices remaining subdued and wage developments continuing to be moderate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the same context the governing council emphasised once again that budgetary positions are still far from being close to balance or in surplus while debt ratios are still at a very high level

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: all the members of the governing council agreed that any tendency to relax the fiscal stance or to alter the strategy enshrined in the stability and growth pact would risk endangering the credibility of the euro and the objective of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on balance the outlook for price stability was judged favourably by the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in an environment of substantial uncertainty monetary policy will be guided by a continuous convergence of central bank interest rates towards the level considered to be appropriate for the monetary financial and economic situation prevailing at the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me now give the floor to the vicepresident to report on various aspects of the preparatory work for stage three of economic and monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 1 revision of the key for the capital of the european central bank ecb revised gdp data which are used to calculate the key for the capital of the european central bank have been received from the commission of the european communities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: when the revisions are applied to the calculation of the capital key variations of more than 001 occur

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: article 2 of the original decision of the governing council of the ecb of 9 june 1998 ecb19981 states that should revisions received before december 1998 result in variations of this magnitude the key for the capital of the ecb may be revised

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the general council and the governing council have therefore considered and agreed to an adjustment of the key and the governing council has adopted the related ecb decision

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: details of the adjusted shares of the national central banks ncbs are presented in a separate press release which is to be issued this evening

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: today also in this connection the general council adopted an ecb decision on the contribution of the noneuro area national central banks to the capital of the ecb for which the adjustment of the key has knockon implications

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the decision states that the noneuro area ncbs will pay up 5 of their subscriptions to the capital of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the four ncbs concerned will not actually be asked to pay their share since the amounts due are less than they can expect to receive as their share in the proceeds of the liquidation of the european monetary institute

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these details were already agreed by the general council at its meeting on 1 september this year and are now contained in a legally binding text

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 2 national legal framework for the monetary policy instruments and procedures in stage three of economic and monetary union as you are already aware from january 1999 the single monetary policy will be defined and implemented by the decisionmaking bodies of the ecb the governing council and the executive board

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the operations of the monetary policy of the escb will be carried out in a decentralised manner by the participating ncbs

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore the ncbs have prepared contractual andor regulatory legal documentation the national legal documentation in order to implement the monetary policy framework of the escb as adopted by the governing council on 11 september 1998 and published in the report entitled the single monetary policy in stage three general documentation on escb monetary policy instruments and procedures

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the national legal documentation of each ncb has been assessed by legal experts from the ncbs and the ecb in order to ensure that it properly implements and complies with the monetary policy framework of the escb which aims at establishing a level playingfield across the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: all eligible institutions wishing to access monetary policy operations and standing facilities in stage three should therefore contact their local ncb in order to prepare for the execution of that national legal documentation in good time before the beginning of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 3 regulation of the european central bank on the application of minimum reserves today the governing council adopted the regulation of the european central bank on the application of minimum reserves

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the final specifications of the minimum reserve system to be used by the escb in stage three was the subject of a press release following the governing council meeting on 13 october this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at that time it was announced that an ecb regulation on minimum reserves would be published shortly thereafter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this commitment has now been fulfilled and the features of the escbs minimum reserve system are contained in a legally binding text

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 4 regulation of the european central bank concerning the consolidated balance sheet of the monetary financial institutions sector today the governing council also adopted an ecb regulation concerning the consolidated balance sheet of the monetary financial institutions mfi sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the purpose of this regulation is to enable the ecb and the ncbs to collect the statistical material required for the establishment of the consolidated balance sheet of the mfi sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the aim of this balance sheet is to provide the ecb with a comprehensive statistical picture of monetary developments covering the aggregated financial assets and liabilities of mfis located in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 5 payments systems issues i legal documentation for the correspondent central banking model ccbm the correspondent central banking model ccbm is a system which will enable all collateral that is eligible for escb monetary policy operations to be used on a crossborder basis

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is a system that relies on bilateral relations between the ncbs involved and implies inter alia a regime of rights and liabilities between the ncbs

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: there are two pieces of legal documentation involved in this issue

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first there is the so called ccbm main agreement which concerns the participating member states and the ecbs and second there is what we call the out ccbm agreement which deals with the regulations for operations concerning nonparticipating member states

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: today the central bank governors of all 15 member states and the president of the ecb signed the out ccbm agreement and the members of the eurosystem signed the ccbm main agreement eurosystem being the term which we now intend to use to refer to the 11 euro area ncbs and the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details of the ccbm and information concerning the forthcoming publication of a brochure on the subject are contained in a separate press release which will be issued to you this evening

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: ii target agreement further to the governing councils agreement on the main features of the legal framework for target in november this year i am pleased to be able to inform you that today the target agreement has been signed by all 15 central bank governors and the president of the ecb thus allowing the noneuro area ncbs to be connected to target

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: by entering into the target agreement today the central banks of denmark greece sweden and the united kingdom have consequently agreed to adhere to the rules and procedures referred to in the target guideline which regulates the relationship between the ecb and all euro area central banks

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: finally it gives me pleasure to announce that the central bank governors of these four countries have committed their ncbs to adhere to the principles laid down in the policy statement on euro payment and settlement systems located outside the euro area which was released to you on 3 november 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: 6 issues relating to accounting and financial reporting finally today the governing council having considered the observations of the general council adopted an ecb guideline on the legal framework for accounting and reporting in the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this guideline will not be published but will be available on request from the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a number of other decisions were also taken regarding the consolidated weekly financial statement of the escb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the formats for the external reporting of the financial accounts of the escb were agreed

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it was decided that friday will be the reporting date of the escb and that publication of the weekly consolidated balance sheet will take place on the following tuesday

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: further details will be supplied when the first weekly consolidated balance sheet is published

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: transcript of the questions asked and the answers given by dr willem f duisenberg president of the ecb question president duisenberg i have a question with respect to point 5 in your statement that says that you decided on a reference rate rather than on a range and the reason you gave was that the council believes that announcing a reference range might be falsely interpreted by the public as implying that interest rates would be changed automatically

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the other hand you said that deviations from this reference rate will not be followed mechanistically by you

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and i do not quite see why this should not also apply to a range

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg we simply felt that the announcement of a range was more likely to be interpreted by the public at large as triggering automatic reactions than the announcement of a rate a reference rate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we may have been wrong in that feeling but that was our lets say psychological estimate of public reactions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and then i should like to point out that if you read that press statement you will see the reference rate given as 4 12 and specifically so

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the same reason it has not been given as 45 but rather as 4 12

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question is the harmonisation of tax rates in europe desirable or useful or necessary for the success of economic and monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg whether it is desirable or useful or necessary has not been discussed by the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: if you want my personal opinion i regard it as something that will happen over time

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and over time means that it could take decades a process of tax structures starting to look more like one another without perhaps ever becoming totally equal

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question when you were in london a couple of days ago you said you wanted the ecb to be one of the most open banks central banks in the world

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: yet it is still not your intention to publish minutes to publish votes or to publish inflation forecasts

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: how do you reconcile these two positions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg i reconcile them by not defining openness as publishing everything that would be available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and that openness by the definition of openness is publishing explaining every decision every consideration including the pros and cons

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: to be very open about that and to be frequent and immediate in that openness

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and i think i admit we have been a central bank for only 5 months

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i am still pretentious in thinking that looking at our record of publications etc we already are the most open central bank in the world

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question mr president i have noticed that your comments on the european economy were more cautious significantly more cautious this time than last time and the times before

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and i just wanted to get an indication of the forecast range for gdp growth that you implicitly assumed in your m3 forecast of 22 12 whether that is still your latest forecast and whether there is in that forecast range a trend downwards or upwards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in other words is this currently a symmetric gdp estimate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg very preliminary forecasts for gdp growth in 1999 indicate some slowdown compared with 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in 1998 we already had to lower the estimate slightly from around 3 it would be now in all likelihood be slightly only slightly below 3

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: our very preliminary forecasts for 1999 indicate a range of growth in the order of 2 12 and they also indicate that this slowdown might be temporary that it might pick up somewhat later next year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: but adding to that i think the risks as far as we can analyse and observe them are on the down side

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question translation president duisenberg are there any concerns which you or your colleagues have with respect to the stock of confidence in the euro concerns which we should know about

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: that is my first question

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it has been reported time and again my second question that leading policy makers in italy in france and in germany are saying in small inner circles that they want to draw on central bank reserves to finance additional programmes within the scope of the european employment pact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: if that were so the first policy maker to say so was mr prodi who is no longer in office what position would you take

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg with regard to the first question as to whether is there a certain concern which we have not told you about yet the answer is no

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the concerns we have are implicit in the forecasts or assessments of the outlook as we see it developing in 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: perhaps as i have just indicated in the answer to the previous question there is some concern that there will be some moderation in the rate of growth and that the risks are more on the downside than on the upside

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to the second question i can note that you refer to small inner circles

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i was part of such a small inner circle last week when i attended the meeting of the ministers of finance of the euro11 countries together with the vicepresident and we did not hear any utterances or comments pointing in the direction you suggested

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the contrary we heard a reconfirmation by the ministers of finance of their will to adhere to the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question how do you think the european citizens will feel and experience what will happen after the new year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg they will feel as excited as i feel around the yearend

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i do not know how they will feel

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: what we hope to inspire is that they approaching that day and from that day onwards look to the future with confidence confidence in their own future and confidence in the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question mr president this reference value of 4 12 i am wondering with the changeover to a single currency there has been a lot of talk about a change in this system in structural changes and that could have an effect on the money supply

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and i am wondering what sort of assumptions there are now about how the money supply will be affected

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first are you considering it would be going up or possibly down

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second there has been a lot of talk about the policy mix in recent weeks and i am just wondering what are you assuming in terms of wage agreements with this reference value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we have seen agreements coming through on the order of 35 eg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the chemical industry

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: is this something you are also looking at

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg with regard to the uncertainties surrounding the changeover the structure they pertain not only to the development of the money supply but to one thing in particular ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: also to the velocity of the circulation of money

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the reference value as i told you in my introductory remarks has to be seen as the summing up or the addition of the trend rate of growth of the euro economy which we estimate at between 2 and 25 and with respect to which we have emphasised that if the process of adjustment or change in the supply factors on the labour market structural policies were to continue one could have a higher trend rate of growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: but this trend rate is based on past experience with all the rigidities that were there

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: then we have the trend value for prices which is defined as the rate of increase in the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp a rate below 2

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and finally on the velocity of circulation we are also not quite certain about it

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we estimate that the velocity of circulation is on a slightly downward trend of between onehalf and one percentage point per year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: now it is quite uncertain how the transition to the euro will in itself affect behavioural relations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and in particular more than you suggested regarding the money supply it is quite uncertain what it will do to the velocity of circulation of money

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: so we cannot do anything but assume that the trends in all three areas the money supply prices and velocity will broadly continue in the future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: that altogether forms the basis for our reference value but it also forms the justification for calling it a reference value rather than a target which it specifically is not

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in practice deviations of actual figures from the reference value over the medium term will also be evaluated and judged and can lead but will not necessarily mechanistically lead to monetary policy decisions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question translation mr president in one months time the european central bank will begin to use its powers

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: some economic analysts say that you will then be the worlds most powerful man in the economic field

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: some european governments actually fear that happening

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: how will you respond

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg well i have never regarded mr greenspan as the most important or powerful man in the world and neither do i regard myself or the european central bank for that matter as in qualitative terms the most important man or institution in the world

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we do recognise that through our measures and through our attitude we will have an important impact on the economic climate in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: that is i think that if that climate were to be one of stability continuity and growth then we would be very satisfied and we would be all the more satisfied the greater the extent is to which we can contribute to creating this climate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question translation mr duisenberg what do you think of the idea of the policy mix which oskar lafontaine launched in discussions with his statement that employment policy always also has something to do with monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg no matter which minister brought it up my answer in general is that of course monetary policy and fiscal policy have something to do with employment policy but i cannot but repeat what i have always said and what is said in the treaty namely that the best contribution monetary policy can make to the growth of the economy and to the growth of employment is to create a stable climate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a climate of price stability is the best thing we can deliver and to the extent that we deliver price stability then as the treaty says without prejudice to the price stability monetary policy should and will contribute to the other economic roles as specified in article 2 of the treaty on european union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question you mentioned tonight as you have in the past the importance of euro area governments engaging in structural reform in their labour and product markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: do you see that urging governments to take actions on national territory is an important part of your role and is there a risk youll be seen as interfering in national affairs if you continue to make those kinds of suggestions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg i do see it as an important i should say almost important part of our role

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: because if we dont urge governments to act in that way who else will

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and it is also an important part of our role because it is our task to help create the climate to do just that and we feel not inhibited to point out that role that governments have to play on the basis of our analysis

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: just as little as governments feel inhibited to point out the role the european central bank would have to play

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we listen to one another we hear one another and we hope to come to the correct decision

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question i think there is strong pressure from the politicians especially from the german finance minister and how do you keep the independence of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: could you elaborate what kind of relation will be desirable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg we keep and maintain the independence by strictly adhering to our mandate which includes that we are forbidden to follow instructions or suggestions from others just as others are forbidden even to give such instructions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: apart from that we will never shy away from a dialogue with other responsible authorities a dialogue concerning our and other policies

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: so we do participate in euro11 meetings we do invite the president of the ecofin council to every meeting of the governing council as the treaty prescribes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we do answer invitations and follow up on invitations from the ecofin council to attend their meetings

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we do anticipate so far as it goes even that the president of the ecofin council has the right not only to attend the meeting of the governing council but also to submit a motion for deliberation to the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the only right he does not have is to vote on that motion

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question i wanted to ask you when you said that your discussion about the rate level from the start had deepened on the broad outlook for price developments it sounds as though the outlook is fairly favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: how strongly should one interpret that

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this is one thing i would like to ask you to talk more about

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: duisenberg we have not reached conclusions but we are now only four weeks away from actually entering stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: and before we go into that we have to set the interest rate with which we will enter stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: so it is only logical that our discussion now that the moment of truth draws nearer is intensifying and deepening and i might say livening up

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: but conclusions we are not there yet

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: question during this autumn during the financial turbulence in asia and russia the currencies in the euro area have been relatively stable whereas currencies outside the euro area such as the swedish crown have lowered their value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank tuesday 22 december 1998 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council of the european central bank at which we took the opportunity to finalise a number of issues of a rather technical or legal nature ahead of the forthcoming changeover weekend

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me first turn to the governing councils discussion on recent economic monetary and financial developments and the decisions that the governing council has taken today in the field of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on 1 january 1999 the escb will assume responsibility for defining and implementing the single monetary policy of the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council of the ecb deemed it appropriate to announce in advance the interest rates that will apply to the monetary policy instruments of the escb as from the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this should eliminate any remaining uncertainties about the monetary policy stance of the escb and contribute to a smooth changeover to stage three of economic and monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as you have already been informed the following decisions were taken first the governing council decided to conduct the first main refinancing operation of the escb as a fixed rate tender and to set the level of the interest rate for this operation at 3 in line with the key central bank rates prevailing at the end of stage two

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this operation will be initiated on 4 january 1999 the allotment decision will be taken on 5 january 1999 and the settlement will take place on 7 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the first longerterm refinancing operation will be announced on 12 january

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council today already decided that it will be conducted through the single variable rate auction procedure

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second with respect to the interest rates on the escbs standing facilities which are designed to form a corridor for movements in shortterm money market rates the governing council decided that the interest rate for the marginal lending facility will be set at a level of 450 and the interest rate for the deposit facility at a level of 2

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these are the rates of the escbs standing facilities at the start of stage three ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: third however as a transitory measure between 4 january and 21 january the interest rate for the marginal lending facility will be set at a level of 325 and the interest rate for the deposit facility at a level of 275

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this exceptional narrow corridor of 50 basis points between the marginal lending facility and the deposit facility aims at smoothing the adaptation of market participants to the integrated euro money market during the initial days of monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the maintenance of such a narrow corridor is not desirable beyond the short term since it would hamper the development of an efficient euro area money market

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore the governing council intends to terminate this measure following its meeting on 21 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in summary let me provide the following explanations for these decisions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i will start with issues related to the narrow corridor thereafter i will comment on the level of the interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with respect to the interest rates on the escbs standing facilities which are designed to form a corridor for movements in shortterm money market rates the governing council had to consider two aspects

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: first it needed to signal clearly its monetary policy intentions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these were expressed by setting the rate for the marginal lending facility at 450 and the rate for the deposit facility at 2 for the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: hence the corridor for movements in shortterm interest rates is asymmetric towards the upper boundary

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: determining these rates was also necessary in order to provide successors to the official national central bank rates previously used as reference rates in certain legislation and contracts in some member states

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: second however the governing council also had to consider the possibility that market participants may need some time to get used to the new environment for monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in principle crosscountry deviations of shortterm interest rates will not exist in stage three as intra euro area arbitrage should be expected to prevent this

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the many novelties related to the changeover make it difficult to foresee whether the euro area money market will indeed work in a fully integrated way immediately from the very first day of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for this reason the governing council has decided to use a relatively narrow corridor of interest rates on the standing facilities of the escb in the first three weeks of stage three as an automatic device to reduce the maximum range of fluctuations in the overnight interest rate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: accordingly we have temporarily designed an exceptional corridor of only 50 basis points with the interest rate for the marginal lending facility at 325 and the interest rate for the deposit facility at 275 which we intend to terminate on 21 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: concerning the decision to set the level of the interest rate for the first main refinancing operation of the escb at 3 it may be recalled that on 3 december 1998 in a coordinated decision all national central banks participating in the single monetary policy lowered their key interest rates to 3 with the exception of the banca ditalia which reduced the discount rate to 35

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as explained by the ecb at that time this joint reduction had to be seen as a de facto decision on the level of interest rates with which the escb will start stage three and which it intended to maintain for the foreseeable future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it was based on the common assessment that these interest rate reductions are in line with maintaining price stability in the euro area over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in this connection it is to be pointed out that a rate of 3 is very low by historical standards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this should be seen as clear indication that the escb does not want to give any signal for a further easing in the foreseeable future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at todays meeting taking account of the latest monetary financial and economic data the governing council confirmed these views

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at this juncture there are no signs to suggest either that current rates of increase in the hicp of around 1 would decelerate significantly or conversely accelerate to levels which are inconsistent with the definition of price stability provided by the escb in october 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me provide you with a more detailed record of our assessment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the information coming from the data on monetary aggregates signals a relatively smooth path for m3 growth in 1998 compatible with continued price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular the latest threemonth moving average annual growth rate of m3 stood at around 45

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this was exactly in line with the reference value set by the governing council at its last meeting

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with respect to the other pillar of the escbs monetary policy strategy the broadly based assessment of the outlook for price developments and risks to price stability various indicators confirm the assessment of developments in monetary data

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the further reduction of longterm interest rates by almost 20 basis points since the end of november to a level of 39 on 21 december as well as the downward shift in the yield curve can be regarded as a sign that markets expect the environment of price stability to continue

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: from the point of view of the governing council it is an encouraging signal that financial market participants are apparently prepared to attribute a credibility bonus to our stabilityoriented monetary policy shortly before its official start

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the current juncture the outlook for the euro area economy is still very much influenced by the uncertainties surrounding the evolution of the world economy in 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these uncertainties have affected negatively indicators of industrial confidence in the euro area and have fuelled expectations of a slowdown in economic activity in the short term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: very recently a first estimate of real gdp growth in the euro area in the third quarter of 1998 has been released by eurostat suggesting a growth rate of 24 against the third quarter of 1997

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this would be around onehalf of a percentage point lower than the average growth rate of 3 in the first half of 1998 compared with the first half of 1997

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: other indicators of real activity were mixed up to november

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while order books and capacity utilisation point to a less optimistic assessment of growth prospects consumer confidence remained high and retail sales continued to increase at a broadly stable pace up to september ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the latest month for which data are available

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: also the decline in unemployment after having paused in the summer months resumed with the rate of unemployment decreasing from 109 in september to 108 in october

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the factors underpinning the currently low increases in the hicp continued to include falling energy prices downward movements in producer prices subdued wage growth and slight decreases in unit labour costs

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on balance the overall environment described above does not point to significant upward or downward pressure on prices in the short term as also reflected in all available forecasts for 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: nevertheless factors contributing to risks to price stability on both sides need to be taken into account

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the one hand downward risks relate to the global environment and potential repercussions on the euro area for example via import prices and further pressure on producer prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these developments will be monitored closely

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the other hand unexpected upward pressure on wages and a relaxation of the fiscal stance would clearly alter the general environment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore we will also carefully monitor the outcome of ongoing wage rounds the plans for fiscal policy in 1999 and over the medium term as well as their implementation towards compliance with the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion the actual situation characterised by monetary growth compatible with continued price stability and the absence of immediate upward or downward pressure on prices justifies maintaining the current stance of monetary policy with an ecb interest rate of 3 for the main refinancing facility

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as we indicated in the ecb press release of 3 december 1998 the intention was also to maintain this rate for the foreseeable future

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed monetary policy in stage three starts with interest rates which are very low by historical standards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me now give the floor to the vicepresident to report on various aspects of the final preparatory work for stage three of economic and monetary union

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: as we noted after our last meeting the measure of a narrow corridor is aimed at facilitating the transition to the new regime by market participants

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we therefore confirm our intention to terminate this transitional measure following the next meeting of the governing council on 21 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: the latest threemonth moving average of annual m3 growth rates covering the period from october to december 1998 was 47

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bankthursday 4 march 1999 ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meetings of the governing council and of the general council of the european central bank

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: after a comprehensive and careful examination of recent trends and ongoing evaluations of the economic outlook for the euro area economy there was consensus that some of the risks identified earlier in particular with regard to real gdp growth had materialised in the fourth quarter of 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: there was also consensus that the impact of these developments on the balance of risks for price stability would need to be examined further in the context of the monetary policy strategy adopted by the eurosystem

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background it decided that for the main refinancing operations to be settled on 10 and 17 march 1999 the same conditions will apply as for the previous one ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the interest rate on the marginal lending facility will continue to be 45 and the interest rate on the deposit facility will remain 20

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me report in some more detail on the governing councils deliberations and thereby provide explanations for the decisions we took today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: starting with the monetary developments in the euro area at the start of stage three of emu the broad monetary aggregate m3 expanded at an annual rate of 57 in january 1999 against 45 in december 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this upturn was largely due to an acceleration in overnight deposits

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this in turn may be explained by the low level of interest rates which also contributed to credit to the private sector to accelerate further in january 1999 to 94 which is particularly notable as other indicators of the economy are signalling a slowdown in activity

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: monthly data on monetary aggregates can be volatile

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: m3 growth is therefore monitored on the basis of threemonth moving averages of the 12month growth rate of m3 which stood at 49 in the period from november 1998 to january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this was 02 percentage point higher than the figure recorded in the previous threemonth period and is 04 percentage point above the reference value of 4½

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background and in view of the uncertainty relating to special factors pertaining to the changeover to the stage three environment and the introduction of the euro the governing council does not consider the acceleration of m3 at the start of stage three as a signal of future inflationary pressures

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however a close monitoring of monetary developments in the coming months remain necessary to give more conclusive evidence of the underlying causes and the permanent or temporary nature of the rise in m3 growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: turning to financial indicators euro area capital markets underwent a correction in february which was mainly linked to spillovers from the united states and japan

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the euro area yield curve shifted upwards across the entire maturity spectrum during february

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me also recall that the nominal effective exchange rate of the euro area in early march stood around 1 below its level on 1 february and around 4 below its starting level on 4 january 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time recent developments appear to have led to a reduction in some of the uncertainties surrounding the evolution of the world economy in 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this mainly relates to the strong performance of the us economy but may also be due to signs of improvement in the real economies of some asian

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: nevertheless in the view of the governing council it is too early at present for a truly favourable assessment of the external environment for the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: risks pertaining to external imbalances continuing risk aversion and the corresponding weakness of private longterm capital flows and real investment to emerging market economies will need to be examined closely

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the euro area the latest indicators confirm that those risks which were identified earlier have now materialised to some extent

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: according to preliminary and incomplete data from national sources real gdp growth in the euro area weakened in the fourth quarter of 1998 when compared with the previous quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while more precise estimates will soon become available from eurostat the evidence available suggests that activity in the euro area has been slowing down in recent months

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this is particularly apparent in the production of themanufacturing sector where output in the fourth quarter of 1998 fell by almost 1 compared with the previous quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these developments broadly confirm the pattern observed earlier in industrial confidence which was on a declining trend in the second half of 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the latest data on industrial confidence in the euro area ie

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: those released by the european commission today indicate that industrial confidence has weakened further

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: some recent wage developments in the euro area might have contributed to that

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the level of unemployment has remained more or less unchanged over the past four months

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: finally consumer confidence in the euro area has remained unchanged from the high levels seen at the beginning of the year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: overall with regard to the cyclical situation recent data confirm our earlier expectations that there are still downside risks for output growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council will continue its thorough analysis and very close monitoring of underlying trends and review its broad outlook for the euro area accordingly on an ongoing basis taking into account in a forwardlooking manner the impact of both domestic and external developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: concerning downward risks in particular the slowdown in the euro area economy is a cause for concern

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion taking the latest available evidence into account at todays meeting the governing council confirmed its assessment regarding the outlook for price developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should now like to inform you about some other matters considered today

Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bankthursday 8 april 1999 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me start with the governing councils discussion of recent economic developments and the decisions that the governing council has taken today in the field of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: after an indepth review of recent monetary financial and economic developments the governing council decided that the interest rate for the ecbs main refinancing operations will from next week on be set at 250

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the interest rate on the marginal lending facility will be lowered to 350 and the interest rate on the deposit facility to 150 with effect from tomorrow

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me report in some more detail on the reasons for which the governing council in the context of the ecbs monetary policy strategy deemed it appropriate to lower interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards monetary developments in the euro area the acceleration of monetary aggregates seen in january 1999 was partly reversed in february

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the 12month growth rate of m3 declined from 56 in january to 52 in february

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this largely reflected a slowdown in the high pace of growth of overnight deposits presumably reflecting the unwinding of the influence of some special factors related to the start of stage three and the introduction of the euro

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as the february figures were somewhat higher than those observed in late 1998 the threemonth moving average of m3 growth covering the period from december 1998 to february 1999 still increased by 02 percentage point to 51

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council does not regard current monetary trends as constituting a signal of future inflationary pressures taking into account that the rate of growth of m3 is still close to the reference value of 4½ and considering that it may to some extent mirror the specific environment related to the start of stage three

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council noted that the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp rates of increase for the euro area have now been below 1 for several months and even though some increases are likely to be seen in coming months owing to the reversal of energy price trends the more lasting effect on the outlook for future prices comes from the economic environment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed reflecting the economic environment many projections for future consumer price increases in the euro area have been revised downwards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in our current assessment of the situation it appears unlikely that hicp increases will be out of line with the eurosystems definition of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to financial indicators both bond and foreign exchange markets were lately under the influence of global factors

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: after having risen somewhat in february 1999 in tandem with us bond yields during march euro area government bond yields remained broadly unchanged

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time the us dollar strengthened further in recent weeks in the light of international developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: when looking in some more detail at the evolution of the world economy positive signs relate to the continuously strong growth of the us economy the gradual recovery in some asian countries and indications of a stabilisation in latin america

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however there is no noticeable evidence as yet of a turnaround in japan

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the euro area overall growth prospects worsened towards the end of last year as reported when we met in early march

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the meantime official data confirm that real gdp growth in the euro area weakened in the fourth quarter of 1998 when compared with the previous quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the weakness is particularly apparent in the manufacturing sector where confidence deteriorated further

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: partial information covering a substantial part of the euro area appears to confirm this picture

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: most recent data on total employment in the euro area point to a certain deceleration in net job creation in the last quarter of 1998

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards the latest available data on the hicp the annual increase in consumer prices has remained unchanged at 08 over several months up to february 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: underlying this stable rate of price increases have been offsetting developments at the level of services and goods prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in february services price increases moderated further slightly mainly owing to downward adjustments in prices in the telecommunication area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time goods prices contributed slightly more to overall hicp increases than before due both to price developments for unprocessed food and a deceleration in the fall in energy prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it may be worth noting that goods prices may continue to move upwards temporarily in particular as oil prices increased strongly from midfebruary onwards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: such movements reflect the higher volatility of price changes of some categories of goods in particular imported oil and other commodities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the interest rate decision has been taken in a forwardlooking perspective focusing on the mediumterm trends in inflation and the compatibility of these trends with the eurosystems definition of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council monetary growth is at the current juncture not a risk for future price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the decision taken today keeps monetary policy on a longerterm stabilityoriented course and by doing so contributes to creating an economic environment in which the considerable growth potential of the euro area could be exploited

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: those responsible for other policy areas are urged now even more to take the necessary steps to improve longerterm growth prospects for the euro area through strictly and decisively adhering to the aims of the stability and growth pact and through convincing structural reforms in the economy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should now like to inform you about some of the other matters considered today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council examined the outcome of a test run of the production of euro banknotes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this socalled zero production run involved the printing works of the participating countries

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the main purposes of this test were first to check the compliance of the test banknotes against the technical specifications and second to prove that all printing works are in a position to produce the euro banknotes to the same high quality standards

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the result of this test was positive as only some minor technical specifications need to be modified slightly

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the printing works will now start their final preparations for the commencement of the mass production of the euro banknotes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also decided to establish an analysis centre for counterfeit euro banknotes

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as is already indicated by its name the main purpose of this analysis centre will be to technically analyse and classify new types of printed counterfeits and to store the related technical data in a database

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the analysis centre will be located at the ecb in frankfurt

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bankthursday 15 july 1999 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council of the ecb which was attended by the eu council president mr niinistö and by mr de silguy european commissioner

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council reviewed the main monetary financial and other economic indicators in line with its monetary policy strategy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: the interest rate on the main refinancing operations of the eurosystem will thus remain 25

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the interest rate on the marginal lending facility will continue to be 35 and that on the deposit facility has been kept at 15

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me give you some details about our latest assessment of the monetary policy stance and thereby explain the decisions taken today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to monetary developments in the euro area the threemonth moving average of m3 growth covering the period from march to may 1999 increased slightly to 52 from 51 in the three months up to april

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: consequently m3 growth remained above the reference value of 4½

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the major contribution to the rise in m3 growth in may came from overnight deposits

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with the exception of repurchase agreements marketable securities included in m3 also experienced higher growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the annual growth rate of total credit to euro area residents rose in may from 73 in april to 79

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the pickup in credit growth was visible both in loans and in securitised lending and occurred in respect of credit to both the private sector and the general government

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the growth of loans to the private sector rose to 10 in may stimulated by the further decline in bank lending rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: taken together with the high pace of growth of the most liquid components of m3 this evidence supports the view that households and firms in the euro area do not currently face liquidity constraints

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council this situation is not seen as threatening price stability at present

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however a reassessment may be appropriate if money and credit growth increase further

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: turning to financial market indicators we have seen a significant upturn in longterm interest rates in the euro area since the end of may

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this development was certainly affected by the continued increase in bond yields in the united states over the same period

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: more recently however domestic factors have probably played a more important role in the determination of domestic bond yields than was previously the case

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these factors include financial market perceptions of more evidence pointing to a further strengthening in economic activity in the euro area during the year accompanied by a modest pickup in inflation expectations from the low levels seen in recent months

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the more positive market sentiment regarding the prospects for euro area output growth has also been reflected in a narrowing over recent weeks of the relatively wide differentials between us and euro area bond yields

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: exchange rate developments do not yet reflect these very same factors

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as we have said on earlier occasions the governing council believes that the euro is firmly based on internal price stability and therefore has the clear potential to achieve a stronger external value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council reaffirmed its view at todays meeting that the monetary policy of the eurosystem will safeguard the euros internal purchasing power and will thereby support its international value

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the prospects for a more broadly based and sustained recovery in the world economy have become stronger

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outlook has improved further in particular in relation to expectations of continuously strong growth in the us economy and some tentative indications that the prolonged decline in activity in japan may have come to a halt

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition recent developments in economic and financial indicators for the emerging market economies suggest that a recovery is under way in southeast asia

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover to the extent that the kosovo conflict may have had a negative impact on economic sentiment in a number of countries its end has eliminated a risk to the outlook for economic developments in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as recent developments in latin america indicate the outlook has improved only moderately

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with reference to developments in economic activity in the euro area some important data have been released since our last meeting

Parsed_Text: most notably eurostat has now started to publish euro area national accounts data which are based more closely on data compiled in accordance with the new esa 95 methodology

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: according to these estimates the quarteronquarter rate of real gdp growth increased to 05 in the first quarter of this year compared with 03 in the previous quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at present there is insufficient experience with regard to the properties of the new esa 95 data in particular their susceptibility to revision and some caution should therefore be exercised when interpreting the most recent developments in real gdp growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however further evidence supporting the view that growth will recover in the course of this year is also provided by the recent development of other indicators of economic activity

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: following successive declines the level of industrial production appears to have stabilised in the months up to april

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: given the developments in industrial confidence up to june it would appear that the trough was reached at the end of the first quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this points to a turningpoint in activity in the industrial sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time household sector demand patterns appear to be broadly unchanged as indicated by a still high level of consumer confidence

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore while the signs of recovery are still modest and are not yet reflected in labour market developments recent data appear to confirm the outlook for a continued improvement in the course of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council considers it necessary that other policy areas make a decisive contribution to bolstering confidence in the euro areas growth potential particularly by means of firm structural reform measures to enhance the sustainability of public finances and the efficiency of labour and product markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a lower rate of increase was recorded in may for both processed and unprocessed food prices and for services prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: hence the decline in the overall hicp rate was also reflected in the hicp rate excluding the two more volatile components energy and seasonal food

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these developments have to be seen partly in the context of a oneoff base effect resulting from countryspecific increases in indirect taxes which occurred last year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the expectation remains that over the next few months the rate of price increases will tend to edge upwards mainly reflecting the increase in energy prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion the outlook for the maintenance of price stability in the euro area remains favourable and in line with the eurosystems definition of price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council therefore decided to maintain the prevailing levels of the ecb interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time it noted that the sustained growth of monetary and credit aggregates the slight improvement in output growth in early 1999 the expectation of a strengthening in economic activity in the course of 1999 and a further acceleration next year all indicate that any upward pressures on prices will have to be monitored very carefully
