Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bankthursday 9 september 1999 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meetings of the general council and the governing council of the ecb which were attended by mr de silguy european commissioner

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council reviewed the outlook for price developments and the risks to price stability in the euro area in line with its monetary policy strategy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as a result the governing council decided not to change the prevailing ecb interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me give you some details about our review of the latest information on monetary financial and other economic developments as well as about our latest assessment of the monetary policy stance and thereby explain the decisions taken today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to monetary developments in the euro area the 12month growth rate of the broad monetary aggregate m3 increased from 53 in june to 56 in july 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the latest threemonth average of m3 growth covering the period from may to july 1999 rose to 54 compared with 53 in the previous threemonth period from april to june 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: overall the annual rate of growth of m3 has been moving away from the reference value of 4½ since the start of the year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this upward movement may be explained to a large extent by the very low opportunity costs of holding monetary assets especially the most liquid components but perhaps also by the gradually improving economic conditions in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time the annual growth rate of credit to the private sector remained high even though it declined by 05 percentage point in july to 104

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the monetary policy strategy of the eurosystem assigns a prominent role to the behaviour of m3

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: accordingly recent monetary developments merit close attention

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time taking into account the fact that we are still in a very early phase of monetary union and that figures for broad money growth have been subject to some revisions in recent months shorterterm monetary developments need to be interpreted with caution

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: concerning financial market indicators the upturn in longterm interest rates in the euro area seen since early may continued in august and early september

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: domestic factors seem to have played a dominant role as indicated by the fact that differentials between us and euro area bond yields have narrowed further

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular market participants appear to be increasingly optimistic about the prospects for economic activity in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time expectations for inflation as reflected by inter alia the signs emanating from indexlinked bonds issued in the euro area tend to indicate that markets still expect an evolution of consumer prices which will remain compatible with price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: developments in the world economy continue to show signs of improvement

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: growth in the us economy continues and some positive economic signals have been recorded for japan

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while the outlook for stronger growth in the global economy is also supported by recent developments in other regions notably southeast asia some risks remain primarily in relation to the strength of the recovery in latin america

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards economic activity in the euro area industrial production data up to june point to a further improvement in output growth in the second quarter of this year as has already been indicated by various survey data

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover available evidence in terms of retail sales data and consumer confidence while somewhat more mixed suggest broadly sustained consumption growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these developments are consistent with recently published forecasts which foresee an upturn in economic growth in the course of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the downside risks pertaining to these projections have tended to recede and real gdp growth might eventually turn out to be somewhat higher than currently forecast

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as generally expected consumer price increases as measured by the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp picked up in july with the annual rate of change rising from 09 in june to 11 in july

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this effectively reversed the downward movement in the overall hicp rate which had been evident since april 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while prices for unprocessed food declined further in july this downward effect on the overall hicp rate was more than offset by a stronger increase in energy prices resulting from a continued rise in oil prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we expect consumer price increases to rise somewhat further from their july levels mainly as a consequence of higher oil prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however at this stage we also expect this further increase to level out below the ceiling we have defined as being compatible with price stability over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion the prospects for a sustained economic upturn in the euro area are good as are the chances of continued price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however we remain vigilant taking into account the upward risks to price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular with a view to conducting a thorough assessment of the risks to price stability in the medium term the increase in monetary growth over recent months and the high growth rate of credit to the private sector need to be monitored very carefully

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the shortterm upward pressure on consumer prices which stems from the increase in oil prices over recent months and the lagged passthrough of developments in the exchange rate have to be taken into account

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: if accompanied by continued wage moderation these factors alone should not be expected to threaten the current outlook for price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: accordingly the results of the wage bargaining round for the year 2000 will play a particularly important role for the further assessment of price developments in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the only way to prolong a noninflationary recovery and hence to substantially reabsorb the still very high unemployment is for all responsible parties to act decisively in the near term to increase flexibility in the labour product and service markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this would also be the best way to allow the economy to take full advantage from the present stance of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: taking all this information into account the governing council decided to maintain the prevailing ecb interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition it stressed that low inflation and therefore low interest rates should encourage higher investment helping to prevent the emergence of capacity constraints during economic expansion

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time the expected improvement in economic activity offers greater opportunities to cut fiscal deficits further and to enhance structural reforms

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed the creation of this virtuous circle depends on all policymakers playing their part

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me now give the floor to the vicepresident to introduce three additional topics which we discussed during our meetings

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition to reviewing the main monetary financial and other economic indicators we discussed issues relating to the transition to the year 2000

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we are now approaching the final phase of testing activities in connection with preparatory work for the century date change

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on 25 september 1999 the ecb and the eu national central banks will conduct a demonstration of the target year 2000 compliance in which according to current information several hundred eu credit institutions will participate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: prior to this the ecb and the national central banks have already successfully tested their target components first at the national level and thereafter in crossborder tests

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: to a large extent credit institutions have already taken part in these tests

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in parallel as announced a few weeks ago on 29 june 1999 the ecb together with the national central banks successfully completed the bilateral testing of the escb applications that are necessary for the conduct of monetary policy operations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the testing exercise together with the parallel remedial actions has proved that these systems are year 2000 compliant

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: you may recall that on 15 july 1999 we decided to close target on 31 december 1999 in order to smooth the transition not only for the escb institutions but also for the other financial institutions

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this day can thus be kept free for endofyear operations and for making full backups of the relevant systems

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the area of target as well as in the area of monetary policy implementation and liquidity management we are also reviewing our contingency procedures to minimise any potential year 2000related impact

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it is worth noting that general contingency procedures had already been put in place shortly before the launch of the euro

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition we will use an efficient communication infrastructure between the ecb and the national central banks to monitor developments over the year 2000 transition period

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the ecb will also share information with the joint year 2000 council and will thereby extend its monitoring capabilities beyond the eurosystem to a global perspective

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as far as our monetary policy framework is concerned we are convinced that it is flexible enough and has builtin mechanisms designed to deal with any level of liquidity demand that might arise in the euro markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed should any adaptation be advisable this would be of limited importance and consistent with the overall setup

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we have analysed different scenarios and have come to the conclusion that the eurosystem will be in a position to cope with any potential increase in the demand for liquidity

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the stock of banknotes held by national central banks is sufficient to allow for a considerable additional demand for banknotes in circulation and the amount of collateral available in the eurosystem will be sufficient to allow for the corresponding increase in refinancing needs of the banking system

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we are therefore confident that the eurosystem will continue its operations smoothly on 3 january 2000 after the century date change

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we also reviewed crossborder retail payment services which are essential for the smooth functioning of the single market

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: we believe that citizens and businesses can only benefit fully from the fundamental principles of the free movement of goods services capital and people if they are also able to transfer money as rapidly reliably and cheaply from one part of the european union to another as is now the case within each member state

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: despite the introduction of the euro however there is still a clear gap between the service levels of domestic and crossborder retail payment systems in terms of quality efficiency and pricing

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the substantial disparities between domestic and crossborder services ought now to be reduced and should ultimately disappear

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in order to encourage the development of crossborder payment systems enabling the public to benefit more fully from the single currency the eurosystem has drawn up a set of objectives for crossborder retail payments in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: these will be detailed in a separate press release which will be issued in the coming days

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the eurosystem calls on the banking and payment service industry to fulfil these objectives by 1 january 2002 at the latest

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: finally i would like to inform you that we also discussed issues related to fraud prevention

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i would like to emphasise that the ecb shares the concerns of the european parliament the eu council and the commission about the protection of the communities financial interests against fraud and other detrimental activities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: consequently for the sake of transparency efficiency and accountability the governing council decided to establish an external supervisory committee to enforce an antifraud scheme at the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this committee will establish a cooperative relationship with the european antifraud office olaf

Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank thursday 7 october 1999 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meetings of the governing council of the ecb which was attended by the european commissioner mr solbes mira

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outcome of todays discussion was that the governing council has decided to leave the prevailing ecb interest rates unchanged

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council conducted an intensive discussion of the current monetary policy stance in which it was concluded that the balance of risks to price stability remains on an upward trend

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to monetary developments in the euro area the threemonth average of the 12month growth rates of m3 for the period june to august 1999 increased to 56 from 55 in the threemonth period ending in july 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while a good deal of caution is required when interpreting shortterm monetary developments it should be noted that the 12month growth rate of m3 has displayed an upward trend during 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the high growth of m3 seems to be related to the low level of opportunity costs of holding monetary assets particularly the most liquid components

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: furthermore the gradual improvement in the real economic situation may have fostered the expansion of m3

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: credit to the private sector also continued to expand at a fast rate in august 1999 namely 107

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: since the start of stage three credit to the private sector has been expanding at rates of around 10

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: developments in credit growth in august tend to confirm that the demand for loans remains strong supported by low bank lending rates indicating that euro area residents do not face borrowing constraints

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on balance the governing council believes that monetary conditions especially the sustained growth of m3 in excess of the reference value signal a rather generous liquidity situation in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: longterm nominal interest rates in the euro area continued to increase in september

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while it is likely that this increase is related to expectations of a recovery of activity in the euro area expectations of increasing inflationary pressure may also play a role

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the more favourable expectations for economic development in the euro area are partly connected with a further improved outlook for the world economy as is also reflected in the recent upward revision of the forecast for world growth by the imf

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the growth of the us economy continues to be strong and in japan economic indicators are now more clearly pointing towards an improvement in economic activity

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition in some asian countries the recovery in growth appears to be taking place somewhat earlier than expected

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: notwithstanding individual downside risks in the countries i have just mentioned and a more general uncertainty regarding the recovery in latin america the world economy seems to be set for higher growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as regards economic activity in the euro area some important data have been released since we last met

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a first estimate by eurostat for real gdp growth in the second quarter of 1999 points to slightly lower quarteronquarter growth compared with the first quarter of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however these data do not appear to impinge on the view that there is an upturn in growth in the course of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in fact industrial production data for the period up to july confirm the gradual improvement of recent months and various survey data suggest that there was a further strengthening of output growth in the industrial sector over the summer months

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: evidence for the consumer sector continues to point to broadly robust consumption growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outlook for a continuing improvement in overall activity therefore remains favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in line with our expectations the annual rate of change in the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp saw a further rise in august 1999 to 12 up from 11 a month earlier

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this upward movement was mainly caused by the ongoing increase in oil prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: some counterweight came from a decline in unprocessed food prices and from a lower rate of increase in services prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: largely reflecting this development in services prices the hicp rate excluding more volatile components namely energy and seasonal food declined to 09 in august having risen to 10 in july

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: oil prices continued to increase further in september and given the relatively short time of passthrough to consumer prices expectations of further increases in the overall hicp rate in the coming months have become firmer

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion monetary and credit developments indicate that continuous close attention must be given to upward risks to price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in the light of the mediumterm orientation of the eurosystems monetary policy the rising trend of m3 growth calls for great vigilance on the part of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the recent increase in oil prices will continue to impose additional upward pressure on the hicp

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: seen in isolation the increase in energy prices should have only a temporary effect upon consumer price increases but it is essential that this effect does not trigger wage claims which prove incompatible with price stability in the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against the background of the mediumterm outlook for a sustained acceleration in economic activity decisive structural reform is warranted in order to prevent early upward pressure on prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in fact the governing council sees a strong case for enhancing structural reform in labour and product markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the anticipation of an expected cyclical improvement should not lead to a weakening of efforts in this regard but rather it should be used as a welcome opportunity to make convincing progress

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this together with continued wage moderation and fiscal adjustment in line with the stability and growth pact would greatly facilitate the monetary policy task of maintaining price stability in an environment of stronger growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me now give the floor to the vicepresident to introduce three additional topics which we discussed during our meeting in addition to reviewing the main monetary financial and other economic indicators the governing council formally adopted the decision of the ecb on fraud prevention according to which an independent antifraud committee will be established to enforce an antifraud scheme within the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the committee will be composed of three independent persons of recognised standing and professional experience in the fields of central banking justice and policing

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: within the ecb the directorate internal audit is entrusted with the task of conducting all investigations relating to fraud prevention and detection

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: for the purpose of combating fraud the director of internal audit will report to the antifraud committee

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a cooperative relationship will be established with the european antifraud office olaf

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as i already emphasised at the last press conference the ecb shares the concerns of the european parliament the eu council and the european commission about the need to combat fraud and other activities detrimental to the financial interests of the communities and the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: you will find further information relating to this decision in the separate press release which has been issued today

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: i should also like to mention that the governing council had a preliminary discussion on eu accession countries

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the accession of new members to the european union is an area of development in which the eurosystem will be increasingly involved

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as you are well aware 12 countries are official candidates for membership and negotiations have already started with a first wave of six countries

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the negotiations with these countries are intensifying and the chapters on economic and monetary union and on free movement of capital have been opened this autumn

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the governing council has already considered a number of issues related to eu enlargement in areas of relevance to the eurosystem

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: following a number of bilateral contacts which the ecb has already had this year the meeting in helsinki will be attended by the governors of the central banks of the accession countries

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: it will provide the opportunity to strengthen the working relationships between the eurosystem and the central banks of accession countries and to deepen the dialogue between the two sides

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: finally the governing council approved 21 additional links established between securities settlement systems which can be used for the transfer of foreign collateral in the eurosystems monetary policy and intraday credit operations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outcome of todays meeting was that the governing council has decided to increase the ecb interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the forthcoming main refinancing operations of the eurosystem will be conducted as fixed rate tenders at an interest rate of 30 starting with the operation to be settled on 10 november 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this increase implies an upward adjustment of 50 basis points from the rate of 25 applied to previous such operations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the interest rate on the marginal lending facility will be increased from 35 to 40 and that on the deposit facility from 15 to 20 both with effect from 5 november 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: overall on the basis of prospective developments the governing council considers that todays decision will counter the upward trend of the balance of risks to price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this decision will therefore contribute to sustaining noninflationary economic growth in the euro area over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the main argument for raising the interest rates was the fact that since around the beginning of the summer the balance of risks to future price stability has gradually been moving towards the upside

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in fact the economic situation in spring 1999 had given rise to concern about downward risks and had led to a precautionary interest rate reduction by 50 basis points on 8 april 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the current economic environment is far more favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: moreover several indicators including monetary growth suggest that there is ample liquidity in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: inflation rates are expected to increase gradually in the months ahead mainly as a result of the increase in energy prices earlier this year working its way through to consumer prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the latest data on industrial producer prices confirm this pattern

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: over the medium term however it is important to prevent the availability of ample liquidity from translating into upward pressure on prices

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular an increase in interest rates now should help to counteract further liquidity growth over the medium term and contribute to maintaining inflation expectations safely below 2

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to the perception that an increase in interest rates now would endanger the resumption of economic growth the governing council is of the opposite opinion

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: a timely rise in interest rates will avoid the need for a larger increase in interest rates later and hence will contribute to stronger growth over an extended period of time

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: concerning the size of an increase in interest rates against the background of a fundamentally changed situation the precautionary interest rate reduction made in april 1999 is no longer justified

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: furthermore todays move by 50 basis points appeared to be the best way in which to avoid uncertainties regarding the future course of monetary policy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition such a move is expected to contribute to reducing any uncertainty premia potentially prevalent in financial markets and also to help to contain a possible increase in volatility in money markets towards the end of the year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the strong growth of the most liquid components of m3 is particularly noteworthy suggesting that the very low level of interest rates favoured the strong growth of monetary aggregates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the pickup in economic activity is likely to have further stimulated m3 growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: credit to the private sector also continued to expand rapidly in september 1999 at a rate in excess of 10

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the demand for loans remained strong throughout the first three quarters of 1999 supported in particular by the low level of bank lending rates and the ongoing economic recovery

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: overall these developments indicate a generous liquidity situation in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: euro area financial market developments over the past few months confirm the general change in economic conditions and perspectives for the euro area by also anticipating an acceleration of economic growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this is reflected in the rise in government bond yields and the associated pronounced steepening of the yield curve since spring 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: todays decision should contribute to firming financial market expectations of stronger growth without increasing inflationary pressures

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to economic activity itself current information indeed continues to support the view that there is an ongoing strengthening in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the outlook for the world economy remains positive this mainly relates to the sustained growth of the us economy but also to the apparent strengthening of the recoveries in southeast asia and japan

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: most recent data releases for the euro area suggest an acceleration of real gdp growth rates in the second half of this year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this is indicated by confidence and survey data as well as by production data for the industrial sector extending into the third quarter of the year

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: therefore the prospects for a continued improvement in output growth remain good

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: concerning consumer prices in september 1999 the annual rate of change in the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp was 12 that is to say unchanged from august 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the one hand upward pressures related to the surge in oil prices in recent months and to the rate of change in prices for seasonal food

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the other hand in september the increases in both services prices and prices for nonenergy industrial goods were more moderate than in august

Parsed_Text: in conclusion the downside risks to price stability have disappeared

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: instead monetary developments together with the accumulating evidence of improved economic prospects confirmed the view expressed earlier by the governing council that the balance of risks to future price stability has gradually moved towards the upside

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this assessment argued in favour of adjusting the interest rates within the context of a monetary policy stance which is conducive to maintaining price stability over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: containing inflationary expectations in a forwardlooking manner is decisive for ensuring sustainable growth in gdp and employment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: willem f duisenberg president of the european central bank frankfurt am main thursday 2 december 1999 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen the vicepresident and i are here today to report on the outcome of todays meetings of the general council and the governing council of the ecb the latter of which was attended by mr niinistö president of the eu council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: let me first report that the governing council decided to confirm the reference value for monetary growth namely an annual growth rate of 4½ for the broad aggregate m3

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this decision was taken on the grounds that the components underlying the derivation of the first reference value in december 1998 namely the eurosystems definition of price stability and the assumptions for trend real gdp growth and the trend decline in m3 income velocity have remained unchanged

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as before the governing council will assess monetary developments in relation to the reference value on the basis of a threemonth moving average of annual growth rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council has decided henceforth to review the reference value on a regular annual basis with the next review to take place in december 2000

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: against this background the governing council wishes to emphasise that the trend growth potential of the euro area could be considerably enhanced by structural reform in the labour and goods markets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the eurosystems monetary policy strategy would take such changes into account as appropriate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the derivation of the reference value of 4½ is an expression of a mediumtermoriented approach

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the generous liquidity situation in 1999 will have to be borne in mind

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the ecb will issue a press release today providing some background information on the review of the reference value carried out today by the governing council

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the press release will also recall the role of the reference value within the eurosystems monetary policy strategy

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the governing council also conducted its regular review of the outlook for price developments and the risks to price stability in the euro area this time including a review of the most recent forecasts and projections

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: after this examination the interest rate on the main refinancing operations of the eurosystem was left at 30 and the interest rates on the marginal lending facility and on the deposit facility were maintained at 40 and 20 respectively

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: allow me to outline the main elements of our assessment of the latest information on monetary financial market and other economic developments

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to monetary developments in the euro area the data up to october 1999 which still refer to the period before our decision to raise interest rates confirmed the picture of a generous liquidity situation in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the annual growth rate of m3 in october 1999 was 60

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: this compares with 62 in the previous month

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the threemonth average of the annual growth rates of m3 covering the period from august to october 1999 was unchanged at 60 and thus stood 1½ percentage points above the reference value of 4½

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the growth of the most liquid components of m3 remained very dynamic

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition the annual growth rate of credit to the private sector continued to exceed 10

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: as we have noted on previous occasions these monetary and credit developments are considered to have been driven mainly by the low level of interest rates as well as by the pickup in economic activity in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the initial reaction of euro area financial markets to the eurosystems monetary policy move of last month was favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular this was signalled by the continued decline in longterm government bond yields and the immediate substantial reduction in market uncertainty regarding the evolution of future longterm interest rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: later in november longterm bond yields in the euro area began to rise again gradually in connection with developments in international bond markets and favourable expectations for world growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: indeed the global economic outlook remains positive and the view that the world economy is set for higher growth appears to be shared by the major international organisations

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: at the same time the expectation that growth differentials between the main economic regions will narrow in the course of time is widespread

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: while real gdp growth in the united states is generally expected to ease it is expected to accelerate in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: overall relatively wide growth differentials between the major world economies will give way to a more balanced scenario thereby underlining the potential for the euro to appreciate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: with regard to developments in economic activity in the euro area the latest data confirm a strengthening of growth in the course of the second half of 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in particular production growth in the industrial sector saw a further upturn in the third quarter and various survey data suggest that this will continue in the final quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: all available projections indicate that this upward momentum will lead to an acceleration in real gdp growth from around 2 this year to close to 3 in both 2000 and 2001

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: consumer price increases as measured by the harmonised index of consumer prices hicp have recently resumed their upward trend as expected

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in october the annual rate of change in the overall hicp was 14 up from 12 in september and august owing to higher price increases for food and nonenergy industrial goods

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: the impact of higher oil prices on energy prices in the hicp which had accounted for most of the upward pressure since june 1999 was countered in october by more moderate increases in other energy components

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: some additional counterweight to the upward movement in goods prices came from a further moderation of increases in prices in the services sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in general the overall upward trend is expected to continue until early 2000 as a result of the increase in oil prices since spring 1999

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: forecasts available suggest that price increases will nevertheless remain below 2 in the course of 2000 and 2001

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: however the actual developments will very much depend on the behaviour of a number of factors and in particular on wage developments remaining in line with price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in addition our assessment has to take due account of prevailing uncertainties

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the upside these relate to inter alia the behaviour of money and credit aggregates the developments in oil prices and the path of the effective exchange rate all of which are closely monitored with regard to their impact on price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: on the downside main factors are linked to the effects of deregulation and liberalisation

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in conclusion the current monetary policy stance should ensure a sustainable expansion of noninflationary economic activity in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg
Parsed_Text: in line with its monetary policy strategy the governing council will remain vigilant with regard to any risks to price stability arising either from domestic or from external sources and act in a timely manner

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg

Parsed_Text: the governing council today approved the ecbs budget for 2000 which gives the ecb the green light to recruit further staff needed to support the ongoing activities of the ecb

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Christian Noyer

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: following our regular economic and monetary analysis we have concluded that the current monetary policy stance is appropriate in view of the favourable outlook for price stability over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: accordingly we have decided to leave the key ecb interest rates unchanged

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: interest rates in the euro area are low by historical standards both in nominal and real terms thus lending support to economic activity and helping to safeguard against downside risks to economic growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the governing council will continue to monitor carefully all factors that might affect this assessment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: allow me to explain our assessment in detail

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in the context of our economic analysis the latest data and information continue to suggest that economic growth in the euro area remained subdued in the second quarter of the year after virtually stagnating in the first quarter

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the indicators available broadly point to a stabilisation of activity but there are no signs as yet of an underlying strengthening in production and confidence

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: at the same time financial market developments seem to reflect a somewhat more optimistic assessment of the economic outlook both inside and outside the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: on the whole we continue to expect a gradual strengthening of economic activity in the euro area

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: this should be supported by lower inflation and thus higher real disposable income the low level of interest rates and a recovery in external demand for euro area goods and services

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: this assessment is in line with all available forecasts and projections

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: nevertheless downside risks to this main scenario are still relevant

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: while concerns over the sars virus have faded there are risks relating in particular to the accumulation of macroeconomic imbalances outside the euro area and to the extent of the adjustment still needed in the euro area corporate sector to enhance productivity and profitability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: turning to price developments the outlook over the medium term remains favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: for the remainder of this year annual hicp inflation rates are expected to fluctuate around the current level of 2 the rate recently estimated by eurostat for june

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in early 2004 a significant base effect related to energy prices should lead to a marked fall in annual hicp inflation rates assuming broadly unchanged oil prices and exchange rates

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: subsequently the exchange rate passthrough and a moderate economic recovery should contain price pressures

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in this respect wage developments in particular are expected to remain consistent with a favourable outlook for price stability

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: other price indicators such as developments in producer prices tend to support this picture

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: moreover all available forecasts and projections as well as indicators of inflation expectations point in the same direction namely that price stability in line with our aim of inflation below but close to 2 will be maintained over the medium term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in the context of our monetary analysis substantial excess liquidity has accumulated in the euro area as a consequence of the extended period of high m3 growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: this strong growth has continued in recent months as economic uncertainty and the low level of interest rates across the whole maturity spectrum have increased the attractiveness of holding liquid assets

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: at the same time the low level of interest rates has helped support recent growth in loans to the private sector

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: while the large amount of excess liquidity should be less of a concern in a period of moderate economic activity monetary developments need to be closely monitored in terms of their implications for price stability over the medium to long term

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: to sum up our economic analysis confirms the expectation that price dynamics will remain moderate in the euro area in the context of a gradual economic recovery and the strengthened euro exchange rate

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the monetary analysis indicates that the strong expansion of m3 should for the time being not be seen as adversely affecting this outlook

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: hence crosschecking the information from the two pillars leads to the conclusion that the outlook for price stability over the medium term remains favourable

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: with mediumterm inflation expectations firmly anchored at levels consistent with price stability and with interest rates at historical lows monetary policy has made a significant contribution to improving the conditions for a recovery in economic growth

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: however other policymakers also have to assume their responsibilities

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: a strong commitment to the stability and growth pact and adherence to well designed mediumterm fiscal consolidation strategies in those countries currently struggling with increasing fiscal imbalances would make a major contribution to improving confidence

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in a similar way progress in structural reforms in the labour and product markets would not only increase the euro areas growth potential and enhance its ability to better withstand external shocks but it would also eliminate a great deal of the uncertainty currently clouding longterm planning and prospects

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in the current situation characterised by subdued economic growth and low confidence structural reform and a steady and reliable course of fiscal policy in line with the european fiscal framework are of the highest priority

Parsed_Text: with a transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen i would like to report on the outcome of todays meeting of the governing council of the ecb

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: today the governing council decided to leave the key ecb interest rates unchanged

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: following our regular economic and monetary analysis we concluded that the current level of ecb interest rates remains appropriate as the mediumterm outlook for price stability continues to be favourable

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the historically low interest rates are lending support to economic activity

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the governing council will carefully monitor all factors that might affect this assessment

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: i will now explain the considerations underlying our decision in more detail

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: starting with the economic analysis recent data confirm that real economic activity in the euro area was very weak in the second quarter of 2003 with the eurostat flash estimate suggesting zero quarterly real gdp growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: however survey data which indicate that confidence is growing as well as recent financial market developments are in line with our main scenario of a gradual upturn in economic activity

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in line with available forecasts and projections we continue to expect this upturn to start in the second half of the year and then to strengthen further in the course of 2004

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the factors supporting the expected pickup in activity are both external and domestic

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: as regards external factors recent data signal that a recovery is already underway in several parts of the world

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: this should lead to an increase in euro area export demand counteracting the effects of the loss of price competitiveness

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: on the domestic side ongoing adjustment efforts by companies to enhance competitiveness and profitability should improve the conditions for an economic upswing

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in this environment the low level of interest rates is strengthening incentives to invest

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: furthermore real disposable income in the euro area should be positively affected by termsoftrade effects stemming from the past appreciation of the euro

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: downside risks to this main scenario for economic growth have declined over the past couple of months but have not disappeared

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: macroeconomic imbalances in some regions of the world persist

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: although these may not affect the shortterm economic dynamics they constitute risks over the longer run

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in addition high oil price levels may continue to have adverse effects on economic activity in the euro area

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: as regards price developments eurostats flash estimate for annual hicp inflation in august was 21

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: while recent oil price developments imply some shortterm upward pressure on inflation rates the broad picture of annual hicp inflation hovering around 2 during the remainder of this year remains unchanged

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in 2004 annual inflation rates should fall below 2 stabilising at levels consistent with price stability

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: this expectation is based on the assumption of moderate wage developments in the context of a gradual economic recovery

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: moreover the significant past strengthening of the external value of the euro should continue to have lagged effects which will limit upward pressure on prices despite some recent corrections in the level of the euro exchange rate

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: over longer time horizons inflation expectations in the euro area seem to be well anchored at levels below but close to 2

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: turning to the monetary analysis monetary growth remained strong in recent months and there is significantly more liquidity available in the euro area than is needed to finance noninflationary growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in part this is due to past portfolio shifts and possibly to an increase in monetary holdings related to precautionary motives

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: moreover the low level of interest rates has contributed to the high demand for liquid assets

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the current level of interest rates is also counterbalancing the negative impact of subdued economic growth on credit demand

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in fact the growth of loans to the private sector has remained relatively robust since the beginning of the year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: at the current juncture the ample liquidity is not expected to translate into inflationary pressure

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: however monetary growth needs to be closely monitored as the significant amounts of excess liquidity could become a source of concern if they were to persist when economic activity strengthens significantly

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: summing up and crosschecking the information from the two pillars our economic analysis confirms the expectation that price pressures will remain subdued in the coming years in the context of a gradual economic recovery and moderate import price and wage developments

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the strong monetary expansion should in view of the economic situation not be seen as adversely affecting this outlook for the time being

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: overall therefore the mediumterm outlook for price stability remains favourable

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: the governing council took note with great concern of recent fiscal developments

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: in order to maintain the credibility of the institutional and economic underpinnings of emu it is fundamental to abide in all respects by the rules of the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: as concerns the upcoming budget plans for 2004 a correction of excessive deficits within the agreed time frame is essential with an annual structural consolidation effort of at least 05 of gdp for countries with fiscal imbalances

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: fiscal plans need to be part of a comprehensive and credible mediumterm strategy with emphasis on expenditure restraint and growthoriented restructuring

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: sound fiscal policies will help to boost investor and consumer confidence and enhance the prospects for stronger economic growth in the euro area

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: progress in implementing structural reforms is as important as fiscal prudence

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: efforts to bring public pension systems onto a sustainable path and to further develop private pension schemes deserve support

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: at the same time more reforms are needed to reduce structural rigidities in labour and goods markets

Speaker: Lucas Papademos
Parsed_Text: such reforms are essential for addressing what is perceived to be the main economic problem of the euro area namely the high level of structural unemployment

Speaker: Willem F. Duisenberg, Lucas Papademos

Parsed_Text: as regards fiscal policy we would like to reiterate our serious concerns

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: with regard to exchange rates we again particularly stress stability and remain concerned about excessive exchange rate moves

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: starting with the economic analysis the latest data on euro area production as well as survey evidence on business confidence remain consistent with ongoing growth around the turn of the year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: looking ahead the external environment of the euro area should continue to develop favourably

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in particular robust real gdp growth in our major trading partners economies can be expected to support foreign demand for euro area goods and services while export growth may be dampened somewhat by the decline in price competitiveness

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the conditions for an improvement in domestic demand are also favourable

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: investment activity should not only profit from global trends in demand but also from companies efforts to enhance productivity and profitability from the low level of interest rates and from generally favourable financing conditions

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: growth in private consumption which has so far remained rather subdued can also be expected to recover in line with an increase in real disposable income

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this assessment is reflected in all available forecasts from official and private sources and seems to be confirmed by developments in financial markets

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: looking at the risks to this outlook there are no new factors to be taken into account

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: over the shorter term risks remain balanced

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: over longer horizons uncertainties relate to the persistent imbalances in some regions of the world and their potential repercussions on the sustainability of global economic growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this calls for sustainable macroeconomic policies and structural reforms which foster a sound balance between savings and investment in all major partner countries which enhance the production potential in the euro area and which support a further expansion in trade of goods and services at the global level

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: overall the governing council confirmed its previous assessment of a favourable outlook for price stability in the euro area over the medium term

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: let me now turn to the details of our economic analysis

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: according to eurostat in the fourth quarter of 2003 real gdp in the euro area grew by 03 quarter on quarter following growth of 04 in the third quarter

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: these data confirm that a gradual recovery in economic activity in the euro area took place in the second half of 2003

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: more recent indicators point to moderate economic growth also in early 2004

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while growth has been relatively modest so far both external and domestic factors give reason to expect a strengthening of the recovery through 2004 and beyond

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the external side all recent indications confirm that global economic growth in 2004 will be robust and broadly based across different regions of the world

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: overall euro area exports should grow significantly this year and next

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the domestic side the conditions for a recovery in private demand are in place

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: over recent months there have been signs of a stabilisation in investment

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: according to eurostat fixed capital investment grew again in the last quarter of 2003 after recording three successive quarteronquarter declines

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: corporate earnings have generally improved in the euro area following a protracted restructuring of corporate balance sheets over the last few years

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the financing conditions faced by corporations in the euro area are very favourable at present

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: all of these factors should support a further recovery in investment

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: there are also reasons to expect a gradual increase in consumption growth during this year following the subdued developments of last year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in the short term growth in real disposable income is supported by lower import prices and tax cuts while later on the gradual improvement in labour market conditions should become an additional factor supporting income growth and confidence

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the financial situation of households in the euro area is sound not least in comparison with a number of other industrial economies and there is no financial impediment to a pickup in private consumption

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: for all these reasons our main scenario of a continued gradual recovery in the course of 2004 and 2005 remains valid

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this view is shared by available forecasts and projections and is also broadly reflected in financial market developments

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we continue to see the risks to this scenario as broadly balanced

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however there are uncertainties related to euro area private consumption and the persistent imbalances in some regions of the world and their potential repercussions on the sustainability of global economic growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: turning to price developments according to the eurostat flash estimate the annual hicp inflation rate declined to 16 in february 2004 from 19 in january

Parsed_Text: jeanclaude trichet president of the ecbhelsinki 6 may 2004 with the transcript of the questions and answers ladies and gentlemen it is a pleasure to welcome you to our press conference here in helsinki where the governing council of the european central bank met today for the ninth time outside frankfurt

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: let me now report on the outcome of todays meeting

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the basis of our regular economic and monetary analyses we continue to expect that price stability will be maintained over the medium term

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: accordingly we did not change our assessment of the monetary policy stance and left the key ecb interest rates at their current low levels

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the low interest rates across the entire maturity spectrum are also supporting the economic recovery in the euro area

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as always we will continue to monitor carefully all developments that could affect our assessment of risks to price stability over the medium term

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: allow me to elaborate on our decision turning first to the economic analysis

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: regarding the current situation and the very shortterm outlook the conjunctural indicators available still provide mixed evidence

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: all in all they suggest that the recovery of real economic activity in the euro area has continued into 2004 albeit at a modest pace

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: most recent information has been more encouraging with the latest euro area survey data offering more positive signals with regard to the beginning of the second quarter

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while the latest positive signals need to be confirmed by future developments they underpin the expectation of the gradual recovery in the euro area continuing and strengthening over time

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the conditions for such a recovery are in place

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: first global economic growth continues to be robust and world trade has strengthened

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the global economic upturn is broadly based both geographically and across sectors and thus provides a favourable external environment for the euro area

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in this context we expect euro area exports to grow significantly this year and next

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: second favourable financing conditions improvements in corporate efficiency and earnings and the strength of global demand should help investment

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: growth in real disposable income should support private consumption especially since households appear not to face financial constraints that might impede stronger spending

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: over time consumer spending should also be supported by an improvement in labour market conditions

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: these considerations underpin our confidence in a continuation of the economic recovery an expectation which is mirrored by available forecasts and projections

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is also in line with financial market developments over the past few weeks

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: obviously any forwardlooking assessment is subject to risks and uncertainties

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the external side the adverse termsoftrade effects of recent rises in oil and other commodity prices pose risks at shorter horizons while the persistence of global imbalances implies some uncertainties over the medium term

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the domestic side uncertainties surrounding fiscal policy and structural reforms in some euro area countries seem to have contributed to preventing a more vigorous improvement in consumer confidence

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: a continued commitment to and greater clarity about the content and timing of these crucial reforms supported by a better understanding of their necessity and benefits for all citizens would help to resolve this uncertainty and thereby mitigate the associated risks for the euro area economy

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: turning to price developments annual hicp inflation rates will exhibit some shortterm volatility over the coming months as we already indicated on the occasion of previous meetings of the governing council

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: according to eurostats flash estimate annual hicp inflation was 20 in april after 17 in march

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while no detailed information is available as yet the recent rise in annual inflation rates is likely to mainly reflect a strong base effect in the energy component resulting from the marked decline of oil prices a year ago

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: moreover recent oil price increases have exerted additional upward pressure

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as these factors will also play a role in the next few months inflation rates of 2 or somewhat above are possible over the short term

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: despite these recent less positive developments over longer horizons we expect inflation rates to remain in line with price stability

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in particular wage developments should remain moderate

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: our outlook for price developments is in line with available forecasts and projections

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however at the current juncture the increase in commodity prices in general and oil prices in particular may pose an upside risk to price stability

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it will therefore remain important to pay close attention to inflation expectations

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: moving on to the monetary analysis annual m3 growth has moderated only slowly since the summer of 2003

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while there is evidence of continued portfolio shifts out of m3 into longerterm assets the pace of this adjustment remains modest

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: both monetary and credit growth continue to be supported by the historically low level of interest rates in the euro area and may also reflect the improvement in the economic environment over the last few quarters

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: given the continued strength of monetary growth liquidity conditions remain ample in the euro area

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the impact of this high level of liquidity on inflation over the medium term will depend on future developments in the economy and financial markets

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: to sum up the economic analysis indicates that the main scenario for the outlook for price developments over the medium term is in line with price stability

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: crosschecking with the monetary analysis does not alter this view at the current juncture

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as usual i also wish to make a few remarks regarding other policies in the euro area

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: with regard to fiscal policies the governing council sees increased reasons for concern

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the basis of the latest commission forecasts the average euro area budgetary position is not expected to improve much this year or next

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: a growing number of countries are likely to report significant imbalances while fiscal consolidation efforts might fall short of commitments

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is essential that all countries concerned undertake credible measures to address these concerns

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: such measures should be part of a comprehensive reform strategy

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this would underpin the ongoing economic upswing by boosting confidence in sound public finances and by improving the prospects for future economic growth

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the governing council welcomes the decision by the commission to request more consolidation efforts from a number of countries

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: turning to structural reforms the governing council reaffirms its view that such reforms are essential if the euro areas growth potential is to expand substantially

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in particular both our employment rate and our labour productivity growth need to increase significantly

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: following our discussions here in finland let me stress that this requires a strengthened technological and scientific base and its application in the euro area as a whole fostered by major efforts to enhance the human capital of our economy

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in this context we are particularly concerned that youth unemployment remains high in several countries

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in order to achieve these goals it is necessary to strengthen the implementation of structural reforms both at the european and the national level

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the lisbon agenda provides an excellent diagnosis of the problem and we have a good understanding of the measures needed to deal with it

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we strongly support the ongoing reforms which should be speeded up across the euro area

Speaker: Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is important to understand that everyone will be better off with higher growth and more jobs if and when the reforms of the lisbon agenda are delivered

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in assessing these risks however it should be taken into account that when expressed in euro the recent rise in oil prices has been significantly smaller than in previous episodes when oil price increases had a major impact on the world economy

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: eurostats flash estimate for annual hicp inflation in august was 23 unchanged from july on the basis of current market expectations for oil prices it appears unlikely that annual inflation rates will return to levels below 2 in the remainder of this year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: looking ahead however there are no indications at present of stronger underlying inflationary pressures building up domestically

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the ecb staff projections for inflation are broadly consistent with other recently released forecasts

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however several upward risks to the projections for inflation exist

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: indeed upside risks to inflation are also reflected in the continued elevated levels of measures of longterm inflation expectations derived from financial market indicators

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: turning to the monetary analysis the annual rate of m3 growth has moderated significantly since the summer of 2003

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this moderation largely represents a normalisation of portfolio allocation behaviour following the easing of the exceptional economic and financial uncertainty which prevailed between 2001 and early 2003

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: nonetheless m3 growth remains resilient

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it appears that the reversal of past portfolio shifts is proceeding more slowly than would have been expected on the basis of historical regularities

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this may reflect an increased risk aversion of households and firms given the stock market losses they experienced between 2000 and the spring of 2003

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: there remains substantially more liquidity in the euro area than is needed to finance noninflationary growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: to sum up while the economic analysis indicates that prospects are consistent with price stability being maintained over the medium term a number of upside risks need to be carefully monitored

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
