Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: then there is the definitive report based on work to continue very actively in a number of domains and that would be presented at the following meeting of the g7 which will take place in washington on the occasion of the imfworld bank spring meetings

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as regards the question on the private sector i would say that my own position is that in a number of domains it is very good that you ask the private sector to work out what would be the code of appropriate conduct or whatever you call it set of principles benchmark principles that would be considered by the industry as being the appropriate fit and proper conduct in a number of domains

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we utilised this methodology after the asian crisis and it worked well in a number of domains

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we have utilised this methodology recently in the domain of the sovereign risks to prevent or tackle a crisis eg

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we have the possibility of debt risk scheduling and so forth and it worked well and we have principles that are agreed upon by a very large number of countries and private sector participants

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so its a good methodology that does not exclude that if it is impossible for the private sector to deliver or if the delivery is not convincing or if again it is impossible to have a consensus of the market participants and of the private sector entities then of course it is always possible and in some cases very important and useful to embark on regulation thats clear

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: now of course regulations themselves which exist in terms of banking prudentials of insurance prudentials of market prudentials and market surveillance and so forth have to be permanently updated and upgraded themselves and we did that after the asian crisis we certainly have to do that taking into account the present turbulences and it is a work in progress so again we have to progress on a very large front the rules and regulations have to be improved to be up to date with our observations

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the experience that we have today shows that we are certainly not at the optimum and because of that we have to make progress on a large front also with the private sector and again not excluding regulation give the private sector a chance to work out itself what would be in its view its own selfregulation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: question i would just like to follow up on what you just said on banking regulation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: would you subscribe to the view that a possible route might be to increase capital requirements for banks as the german finance ministry and also alan greenspan have indeed suggested

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and the second question is on fiscal policy

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: you have been very categorical in rejecting the usefulness of discretionary fiscal policy

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the us is just about to implement a discretionary fiscal package which was supported by a large number of economists international institutions and even the fed

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: does your rejection of this instrument have to do with the fact that the european economy might react differently from the us economy to such packages or is it that you have a different view of how the economy operates

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: trichet on the first question i do not want to launch into the discussions that take place in the basel committee chaired by nout wellink the governor of the central bank of the netherlands and the work of the financial stability forum which is also examining the report of the basel committee

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so i think that we have to be very careful in this respect and see what would be the provisional and when the time comes definitive conclusion of these discussions

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: what is clear in my opinion is that we have through the banking prudentials as well as through all other possible grids to look at what is procyclical in the present set of rules and behaviour and try to avoid procyclicality because one of the lessons of the present observations is that there is probably a tendency for parts of global finance to be much too procyclical

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so i do not exclude the possibility that some changes will be proposed in order to be less procyclical

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: but as you know under the present basel ii agreement there is certainly always a possibility for the banking surveillance authority to augment the capital requirement according to pillar 2 on top of what would be suggested by pillar 1 which is the computation of the appropriate capital requirement whether you use a sophisticated methodology or a more standard methodology

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: but in any case you always have the possibility on the basis of an assessment made by the surveillance authority to increase the capital requirements

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so this particular point is already embedded in the present methodology of basel ii

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as regards our fiscal position again i said that for monetary policy we have different economies different features structural features of the economy and different shocks that we have to cope with

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: one important difference between the us and europe which i have to underline at least at the level of the single economy with a single currency the 320 million people that are making up the euro area is that we are balanced

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we are financing our investment with our savings and we have no domestic or external imbalances

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in the us as you know you have a big level of imbalance

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: that makes a difference on the two sides of the atlantic

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i mention that en passant but it is something which deserves to be underlined

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: let me also say that when i look at the level of public spending as a proportion of gdp we are very significantly higher in the euro area in comparison with the us

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so when i say let the automatic stabilisers do their work it means something much more important as a proportion of gdp in our own case than in the united states of america

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so again when you look at the precise situation on both sides of the atlantic you see that you have to take everything into account

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we have to take into account the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is not just a matter of the commission which is the guardian of the stability and growth pact

Parsed_Text: the stability and growth pact has been decided by the governments themselves

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we did not sign the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is not the commission that signed the stability and growth pact

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it has been signed by the governments the unanimous governments of the european union and of course the euro area

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: question i have a question regarding the dollar

Parsed_Text: question just a quick question picking up on something that you said earlier

Parsed_Text: you seemed a lot less convinced that emerging markets growth would offset the declining growth in the us

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: does that mean youve sort of stopped believing in the theory of decoupling

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so is that something that youre concerned with

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: trichet i never subscribe myself to the theory of decoupling

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i always said that we were in a world which was interdependent and that all things being equal of course if any component of the world goes up or down it has an influence on all the other components

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we are ourselves influencing the rest of the world very much the european union is the first commercial entity of the world

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the euro area is a very important commercial entity and from that standpoint we are very much at the level of the united states of america so through the trade channel we have both i would say a great influence

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i think that those who were speaking of decoupling had in mind that you could have simultaneously in the world for instance a business cycle which would be very much on the downside in the united states and a business cycle which would continue to be on the upside in the emerging world particularly in emerging asia but that in my opinion doesnt mean decoupling because its clear that all things being equal if the us had not gone down quite strongly then of course the emerging asia would have gone up even more

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is clear that all elements that we have in mind are confirming that the downside evolution of the real economy in the us is likely even if we have to be totally pragmatic and depending on facts and figurs

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and we will see what happens and what we have today is that china india and the asian countries continue to have very significant dynamism and the offsetting of the us slowdown could be partially or more than partially be done by asia

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: but at this stage i really think that decoupling is not an appropriate word

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we have to take absolutely all elements into account

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as regards your second question on the insurers again you remember we always considered in this press conference that what we were observing was an ongoing market correction with episodes of turbulence and episodes of high levels of volatility and that it was an ongoing correction across a very large array of different markets

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in line with the diagnosis that we made a long time ago before the start of the turbulences and that i reported to you concerning the fact that we had in a large array of different markets an underpricing of risks a level of volatility a level of spreads a level of risk premia which were too low

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: so the fact that this correction continues in various markets is not something which should surprise us its an ongoing process again and i will certainly not call it a tsunami or anything of that sort but i would say that we have to remain very alert

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i said myself that we were continuing to observe this market correction

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: let me say also for your information that we have decided today that we would renew the supplementary longterm refinancing operations of 23 november 07 and 12 december 07

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: you will have a press release providing further information on this decision of the governing council today

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and then second on the refinancing operation my understanding is that the term money market has been relaxed considerably

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: did you see this in line with the strategy of progressively encouraging this trend

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i would be interested in your observation as to whether you have seen this as a positive trend

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: but what i can say is that we are doing our job

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: our job is very important and we take our decisions on the basis of our mandate

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and our mandate price stability permits us very clearly to contribute precisely through price stability which is our primary goal to longterm sustainable growth and job creation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and let me only mention that one of the biggest successes of the euro area in the real economy which is absolutely remarkable since the settingup of the euro is that we have created a huge number of jobs more than in the us to be clear and that the first nine years of the euro have been from that standpoint remarkably successful

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: and i want to insist on that because it is not a wellknown fact

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i would say that on both sides of the atlantic again we are used to observers and remarks and so forth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: i trust that we are doing what is necessary

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: there is a good criteria which is to see exactly what you do in terms of anchoring medium term inflationary expectations and from that standpoint it seems to me that our own results are solid

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: as regards the money market evolution it is true and we are very satisfied with this on both sides of the atlantic that the tensions as far as we measured them have undoubtedly diminished and depending on the measure you could say that they progressively came down from a very high level and now we are as regards the spread between the threemonth rate and the overnight rate in three months time which is a good measure perhaps of the tension we are probably around 40 basis points now

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however having said that we considered that we had to consolidate and to accompany this progressive improvement of the situation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we judged it to be appropriate to renew these longterm refinancing operations

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: question i wonder if you could give us a little bit more insight into the governing councils thinking on discontinuing the swap arrangement with the fed

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: trichet we have mentioned already publicly that we were extremely satisfied with the cooperation we had with the fed in december that it worked very well and it contributed certainly very significantly to the improvement of the situation of the money market and the appeasement of tensions

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we were also very satisfied with what we were doing with the fed and with the swiss national bank in january

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we said that at the present moment after the good results we obtained with this dollar supply on this side of the atlantic taking into account the need of our own market it was not necessary to continue and the swiss national bank made the same observation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we will see what happens and again we are totally pragmatic

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: if at any time it appears that it is opportune to reactivate such a concept we will do it but at this stage it looked unnecessary both for us and for the swiss national bank

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: let me report on the outcome of our meeting which was also attended by mr bajuk president of the ecofin council and commissioner almunia

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the latest information has confirmed the existence of strong shortterm upward pressure on inflation

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it has also confirmed the assessment that there are upside risks to price stability over the medium term in a context of very vigorous money and credit growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: incoming macroeconomic data point to moderating but ongoing real gdp growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: yet the level of uncertainty resulting from the turmoil in financial markets remains high

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: against this background we emphasise that maintaining price stability in the medium term is our primary objective in accordance with our mandate

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: indeed the firm anchoring of medium to longerterm inflation expectations is of the highest priority to the governing council

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we believe that the current monetary policy stance will contribute to achieving this objective

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the governing council remains strongly committed to preventing secondround effects and the materialisation of upside risks to price stability over the medium term

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the latest information on economic activity confirms the picture of moderating growth around the turn of the year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: according to eurostats first estimate the quarteronquarter growth rate of euro area real gdp in the fourth quarter of 2007 was 04 following 08 in the previous quarter

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: surveys of business and consumer confidence which have followed a downward trend since the summer of 2007 overall remain consistent with ongoing growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: looking ahead in 2008 both domestic and foreign demand are expected to support ongoing real gdp growth in the euro area albeit at lower rates than during 2007

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the fundamentals of the euro area economy remain sound and the euro area economy does not suffer from major imbalances

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while being dampened by the global slowdown investment growth should provide ongoing support as capacity utilisation is high and profitability has been sustained

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: at the same time as a result of the improved economic conditions and wage moderation employment and labour force participation have increased significantly and unemployment rates have fallen to levels not seen for 25 years

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: while being dampened by higher commodity prices consumption growth should continue to contribute to economic expansion in line with rising employment

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: these factors are also reflected in the march 2008 ecb staff macroeconomic projections

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: annual real gdp growth is projected to lie in the range of 13 to 21 in 2008 and to be between 13 and 23 in 2009

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in comparison with the december 2007 eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections the ranges projected for real gdp growth in 2008 and 2009 have been revised downwards reflecting weaker global demand stronger pressure from commodity prices and less favourable financing conditions than were foreseen in december

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council uncertainty about the prospects for economic growth remains unusually high

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: downside risks to the outlook for economic activity continue to exist

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: they relate mainly to a potentially broader than currently expected impact of financial market developments

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: further downside risks stem from the scope for additional commodity price rises protectionist pressures and the possibility of disorderly developments owing to global imbalances

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: with regard to price developments according to eurostats first estimate the annual hicp inflation rate was 32 in february 2008 unchanged from january

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: this confirms the strong upward pressure on inflation in the short term stemming mainly from the increases in energy and food prices in recent months

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: looking ahead we expect a more protracted period of relatively high rates of inflation than we did a few months ago

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the annual hicp inflation rate will most likely remain significantly above 2 in the coming months and moderate only gradually later in the year

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the march 2008 ecb staff macroeconomic projections foresee annual hicp inflation of between 26 and 32 in 2008 and between 15 and 27 in 2009

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: compared with the december 2007 eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections the projected ranges for hicp inflation have shifted upwards mainly reflecting significant additional increases in food and energy prices

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: it is important to recall that these staff projections are based on a number of assumptions which are of a purely technical nature and unrelated to policy intentions

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in particular the technical assumptions for shortterm interest rates are taken from market expectations as at midfebruary

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: moreover it should be noted that the projections are based on the assumptions that the recent dynamism in commodity prices will diminish over the projection horizon in line with futures prices and that pressure from labour costs and profit margins will be limited

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council the risks to the outlook for inflation over the medium term are on the upside

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: these risks include further rises in oil and agricultural prices continuing the strong upward trend observed in recent months

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: furthermore they include the possibility that stronger than currently expected wage growth may emerge taking into account high capacity utilisation and tight labour market conditions

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: moreover the pricing power of firms notably in market segments with low competition could be stronger than expected

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: increases in administered prices and indirect taxes beyond those foreseen thus far also pose upside risks to the inflation outlook

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: at this juncture it is imperative that all parties concerned meet their responsibilities and that secondround effects on pricesetting on the one hand and on wages on the other hand stemming from current inflation rates be avoided

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in the view of the governing council this is of key importance in order to preserve price stability in the medium term and thereby the purchasing power of all euro area citizens

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in this context the governing council is concerned about the existence of schemes in which nominal wages are indexed to consumer prices

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: such schemes involve the risk of upward shocks in inflation leading to a wageprice spiral which would be detrimental to employment and competitiveness in the countries concerned

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the governing council therefore calls for such schemes to be avoided

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: annual m3 growth remained very vigorous at 115 in january supported by the continued strong growth of mfi loans to the private sector

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: a number of temporary factors suggest that m3 growth currently overstates the pace of the underlying monetary expansion

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: the relatively flat yield curve in particular has made holding monetary assets more attractive

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however even after taking such effects into account a broadbased assessment of the latest data confirms that the underlying rate of money and credit growth remains strong

Parsed_Text: the growth of household borrowing has moderated over recent months reflecting the impact of higher key ecb interest rates since december 2005 and cooling housing markets in several parts of the euro area

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: however the growth of loans to nonfinancial corporations has remained very robust

Parsed_Text: bank borrowing by euro area nonfinancial corporations grew at an annual rate of 146 in the year to january 2008

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: overall bank loans to the domestic private sector have grown at around 11 on an annual basis for the past two years

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: for the time being there is little evidence that the financial market turbulence since early august 2007 strongly influenced the overall dynamics of broad money and credit aggregates up to january 2008

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: in addition according to the available data the turmoil has not led to substantial portfolio shifts into monetary assets as were observed between 2001 and 2003

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: notwithstanding the tightening of credit standards reported in the bank lending survey for the euro area continued strong loan growth to nonfinancial corporations suggests that the supply of bank credit to firms in the euro area has not been significantly impaired by the financial turmoil thus far

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: to sum up a crosscheck of the outcome of the economic analysis with that of the monetary analysis fully confirms the assessment that there are upside risks to price stability over the medium term in a context of very vigorous money and credit growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: we emphasise that the firm anchoring of medium to longerterm inflation expectations is of the highest priority to the governing council

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: regarding fiscal policies the governing council welcomes the fact that the berlin eurogroup agreement of april 2007 including the consolidation targets was confirmed in the ecofin councils opinions on the latest stability programme updates

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: there is no justification for delaying structural fiscal consolidation in countries with remaining fiscal imbalances

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: on the contrary the challenges ahead call for particularly prudent and stabilityoriented fiscal policies to support private sector confidence

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: achieving and maintaining sound fiscal positions will also allow the free operation of automatic stabilisers and contribute to the smooth functioning of economic and monetary union

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: structural reforms would not only be beneficial for employment and potential growth but would also help to reduce inflationary pressures

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
Parsed_Text: enhancing competition especially in services and network industries is essential at this juncture to support price stability and enhance productivity growth

Speaker: Lucas Papademos, Jean-Claude Trichet
